   325	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   328	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   329	      else false

   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   440	-/
   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   482	-/
   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      if tA = tB then
   534	        decide (a = b)
   535	      else
   536	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   537	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   538	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   539	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   540	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   541	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   542	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   543	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   544	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   545	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   546	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   547	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   548	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   549	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   550	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   551	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   552	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   553	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   554	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   555	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   556	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   557	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   563	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   564	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   565	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   566	          else true
   567	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   568	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   569	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   570	          else true
   571	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   572	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   573	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   574	          else true
   575	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   576	    else false
   577	
   578	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   579	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   580	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   581	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   582	-/
   583	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   584	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   585	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   586	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   587	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   588	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   589	  μ_prob := by sorry
   590	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

     6	/-!
     7	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     8	
     9	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
    10	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
    11	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
    12	needed by later formalization stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    17	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
    18	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
    19	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    32	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    33	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    34	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    35	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    36	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    37	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    38	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    39	-/
    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    49	
    50	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    51	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    52	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    59	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    61	-/
    62	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    63	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    64	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    65	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    66	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    67	      fun x =>
    68	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    69	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    70	
    71	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    72	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    73	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    74	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    75	-/
    76	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    78	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    79	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    80	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    81	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    82	
    83	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    84	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    87	-/
    88	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    89	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    90	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    91	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    92	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    93	
    94	/--
    95	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    96	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    98	-/
    99	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   100	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   104	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   109	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   110	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   111	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   112	
   113	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   114	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   115	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   116	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   117	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   119	-/
   120	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   121	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   122	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   123	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   124	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   125	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   126	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   127	
   128	/--
   129	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   130	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, with
   131	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   132	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the
   133	level proof remains deferred in this skeleton.
   134	-/
   135	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   136	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   137	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   138	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   139	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   140	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   141	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   142	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   143	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   144	  sorry
   145	
   146	/--
   147	The graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge
   148	`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
   149	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
   150	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   151	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   155	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   156	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   157	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   158	
   159	/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
   160	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   161	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   162	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   163	  sorry
   164	
   165	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    76	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    78	-/
    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80	
    81	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97	
    98	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   100

   102	
   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   122	
   123	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate

   653	\subsubsection{Bit string representations}
   654	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   655	
   656	As mentioned at the end of \Cref{sec:tms}, we sometimes treat the
   657	inputs and outputs of Turing machines as representing elements of a finite
   658	field, or a vector space over a finite field.
   659	We discuss some important details about bit representations of finite field
   660	elements and arithmetic over finite fields.
   661	
   662	In the paper we only consider fields $\F_{2^k}$ where $k$ is odd. 
   663	
   664	\begin{definition}\label{def:admissible-size}
   665	  A field size $q$ is called an \emph{admissible} field size if $q=2^k$ for odd
   666	  $k$.
   667	\end{definition}
   668	
   669	Elements of $\F_2$ are naturally represented using bits. 
   670	To represent elements of $\F_{2^k}$ as binary strings we require the
   671	specification of a basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   672	Given a basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{2^k}$, every element $a \in \F_{2^k}$
   673	has a unique expansion $a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i$ and can be represented as the
   674	$k$-bit string corresponding to $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$.
   675	Note that we omitted the subscript $2$ of $\downsize$ as it maps to the linear
   676	space over the prime subfield $\F_2$.
   677	Thus the \emph{binary representation} of $a \in \F_{2^k}$ is defined as the
   678	natural binary representation of $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$ (which in turn is the
   679	\emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}).
   680	Throughout the paper we freely associate between the binary representation of a
   681	field element $a \in \F_{2^k}$ and its $\F_2$-representation,
   682	although---technically speaking---these are distinct objects.
   683	
   684	Given the representations $\downsize(a), \downsize(b)$ of $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$, to
   685	compute the binary representation of $a+b$ it suffices to compute the addition
   686	bit-wise, modulo $2$.
   687	Computing the multiplication of elements $a, b$ requires the specification of
   688	the multiplication tables $\{K_{e_i} \in \Matrix_k (\F_2)\}_{i=1}^k $ for the
   689	basis $\{e_i\}$.
   690	Given representations $\downsize(a) = (a_i)_{i=1}^k$, $\downsize(b) =
   691	(b_i)_{i=1}^k$ for $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$ respectively, the representation
   692	$\downsize(ab)$ of the product $ab$ is computed as
   693	\begin{equation}
   694	  \label{eq:eq-mult}
   695	  \downsize(ab) = \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \, \downsize \bigl( e_i b \bigr) =
   696	  \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \bigl( K_{e_i}\, \downsize (b) \bigr)\;.
   697	\end{equation}
   698	Thus, using our representation for field elements, efficiently performing finite
   699	field arithmetic in $\F_{2^k}$ reduces to having access to the multiplication
   700	table of some basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   701	
   702	The following fact provides an efficient deterministic algorithm for computing a
   703	self-dual normal basis for $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the corresponding
   704	multiplication tables for any odd $k$.
   705	
   706	\begin{lemma}
   707	  \label{lem:efficient_basis}
   708	  There exists a deterministic algorithm that given an odd integer $k > 0$,
   709	  outputs a self-dual normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the
   710	  multiplication tables of the basis in $\poly(k)$ time.
   711	\end{lemma}
   712	
   713	\begin{proof}
   714		The algorithm of Shoup~\cite[Theorem 3.2]{shoup1990new} shows that for prime
   715	  $p$, an irreducible polynomial in $\Fp[X]$ of degree $k$ can be computed in
   716	  time $\poly(p, k)$.
   717	  Then, the algorithm of Lenstra~\cite[Theorem 1.1]{lenstra1991finding} shows
   718	  that given such an irreducible polynomial, the multiplication table of a
   719	  normal basis of $\F_{p^k}$ over $\Fp$ can be computed in $\poly(k,\log p)$
   720	  time.
   721	  Finally, the algorithm of Wang~\cite{wang1989algorithm} shows that for odd $k$
   722	  and a multiplication table $K$ of a normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$, a
   723	  multiplication table $K'$ for a self-dual normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over
   724	  $\F_2$ can be computed in $\poly(k)$ time.
   725	  Putting these three algorithms together yields the claimed statement.
   726	\end{proof}

  1052	\subsection{Generalized Pauli observables}
  1053	\label{sec:generalized-pauli}
  1054	
  1055	
  1056	For prime number $p$, the generalized Pauli operators over $\Fp$ are a
  1057	collection of observables indexed by a basis setting $X$ or $Z$ and an element
  1058	$a$ or $b$ of $\Fp$, with eigenvalues that are $p$-th roots of unity.
  1059	They are given by
  1060	\begin{equation}
  1061	  \label{eq:pauli-fp}
  1062	  \sigma^X(a) = \sum_{j \in \Fp} \ket{j + a} \bra{j}\qquad \text{and} \qquad
  1063	  \sigma^Z(b) = \sum_{j \in \Fp} \omega^{bj} \ket{j} \bra{j}\;,
  1064	\end{equation}
  1065	where $\omega = e^{\frac{2\pi i}{p}}$, and addition and multiplication are over
  1066	$\Fp$.
  1067	These observables obey the ``twisted commutation'' relations
  1068	\begin{equation}
  1069	  \label{eq:twisted-fp}
  1070	  \forall a,b\in\Fp\;,\qquad \sigma^X(a)\, \sigma^Z(b) =
  1071	  \omega^{-ab} \,\sigma^Z(b)\,\sigma^X(a)\;.
  1072	\end{equation}
  1073	Similarly, over a field $\Fq$ with $q$ a power of $p$, we can consider a set of generalized Pauli
  1074	operators, indexed by a basis setting $X$ or $Z$ and an element of $\Fq$ and
  1075	with eigenvalues that are $p$-th roots of unity.
  1076	For $a, b\in\Fq$ they are given by
  1077	\begin{equation*}
  1078	  \qp^X(a) = \sum_{j \in \Fq} \ket{j+a}\bra{j} \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  1079	  \qp^Z(b)= \sum_{j \in \Fq} \omega^{\tr(b j)} \ket{j}\bra{j}\;,
  1080	\end{equation*}
  1081	where addition and multiplication are over $\Fq$.
  1082	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $a, a' \in \Fq$, and $b \in \Fp$, powers of these
  1083	observables obey the relations
  1084	\begin{equation*}\label{eq:pauli-product-power}
  1085	  \bigl(\qp^W(a)\qp^W(a')\bigr) = \qp^W(a+a') \qquad \text{and}
  1086	  \qquad \bigl( \qp^W(a) \bigr)^b = \qp^W(a b) \;.
  1087	\end{equation*}
  1088	In particular, since $pa=0$ for any $a\in \Fq$ we get that that $(\qp^W(a))^p =
  1089	I$ for any $a\in\Fq$.
  1090	The observables obey analogous ``twisted commutation'' relations
  1091	to~\eqref{eq:twisted-fp},
  1092	\begin{equation}
  1093	  \label{eq:twisted-fq}
  1094	  \forall a, b \in \Fq\;, \qquad \qp^X(a)\, \qp^Z(b) =
  1095	  \omega^{-\tr(a b)} \, \qp^Z(b)\, \qp^X(a)\;.
  1096	\end{equation}
  1097	It is clear from the definition that all of the $\qp^X$ operators commute with
  1098	each other, and similarly all the $\qp^Z$ operators commute with each other.
  1099	Thus, it is meaningful to speak of a common eigenbasis for all $\qp^X$
  1100	operators, and a common eigenbasis for all $\qp^Z$ operators.
  1101	The common eigenbasis for the $\qp^Z$ operators is the computational
  1102	basis $\{\ket{j}\}_{j \in \F_q}$.
  1103	To map this basis to the common eigenbasis of the $\qp^X$ operators, one can
  1104	apply the Fourier transform
  1105	\begin{equation}
  1106	  \label{eq:fourier-f}
  1107	  F \,=\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{q}} \sum_{a, b\in \Fq} \omega^{-\tr(ab)}
  1108	  \ket{a}\bra{b}\;.
  1109	\end{equation}
  1110	Explicitly, the eigenbases consist of the vectors $\ket{e_W}$ labeled by an
  1111	element $e \in \Fq$ and $W \in \{X, Z\}$, given by
  1112	\begin{equation*}
  1113	  \ket{e_X} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{q}} \sum_j \omega^{- \tr(e j)} \ket{j}\;, \qquad
  1114	  \ket{e_Z}   = \ket{e}\;.
  1115	\end{equation*}
  1116	We denote the POVM whose elements are projectors onto basis vectors of the
  1117	eigenbasis associated with the observables $\qp^W$ by $\{\qp^W_e\}_e$.
  1118	Then for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $a\in \Fq$, the observables $\qp^W(a)$ can be
  1119	written as
  1120	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}
  1121	  \qp^W(a) = \sum_{b \in \Fq} \omega^{\tr(a b)} \qp^W_b\;.
  1122	\end{equation}
  1123	
  1124	To invert this relation, we first quote the following useful Fourier fact.
  1125	\begin{lemma}[Fact 3.2 of \cite{NW19}]
  1126	  \label{lem:cancellation}
  1127	  Let $V$ be a subspace of $\F^k$. For all $v \not\in V^\perp$, 
  1128	  \begin{equation*}
  1129	    \E_{u \sim V} \omega^{\tr(u \cdot v)} = 0\;,
  1130	  \end{equation*}
  1131	  where the expectation is over a uniformly random vector $u$ from $V$.
  1132	\end{lemma}
  1133	
  1134	We may now invert~\Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}:
  1135	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-inversion-0-single}
  1136	  \E_{a\in \F_q} \omega^{-\tr(ab)} \qp^W(a) = \sum_{b'\in \F_q} \E_{a\in \F_q}
  1137	  \omega^{\tr(a(b'-b))} \qp^W_{b'} = \qp^W_b\;,
  1138	\end{equation}
  1139	where the second step follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}.
  1140	
  1141	For systems with many qudits, we will consider tensor products of the operators
  1142	$\qp^W$.
  1143	Slightly abusing notation, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$ and $a \in \Fq^n$ we denote by
  1144	$\qp^W(a)$ the tensor product $\qp^W(a_1) \ot \dots \ot \qp^W(a_n)$.
  1145	These obey the twisted commutation relations
  1146	\begin{equation*}
  1147	  \forall a,b\in \Fq^n,\qquad \qp^X(a)\, \qp^Z(b) \,=\, \omega^{-\tr (a \cdot
  1148	    b)}\, \qp^Z(b)\, \qp^X(a)\;,
  1149	\end{equation*}
  1150	where $a \cdot b = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i b_i \in \Fq$.
  1151	For $W\in\{X,Z\}$ and $e \in \Fq^n$ define the eigenstates
  1152	\[ \ket{e_W} = \ket{(e_1)_W} \ot \dots \ot \ket{(e_n)_W}\;, \]
  1153	and associated rank-$1$ projectors $\qp^W_e$. Analogous versions of \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}
  1154	and \Cref{eq:pauli-inversion-0-single} relate the multi-qubit observables

  1157	  \qp^W(a) &= \sum_{b \in \Fq^n} \omega^{\tr(a \cdot b)}

  1159	    \E_{a\in \F_q^n} \omega^{-\tr(a \cdot b)} \qp^W(a) &= \sum_{b'\in \F_q^n} \E_{a\in \F_q^n}
  1160	  \omega^{\tr(a\cdot (b'-b))} \qp^W_{b'} = \qp^W_b\;. \label{eq:pauli-inversion-0}
  1161	\end{align}

215	\subsection{Distance measures}
   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)
   230	\end{definition}
   231	
   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}
   241	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}
   244	    = O(\delta)\;.\footnote{Here the use of the $O(\cdot)$ notation refers to the fact that the notation will often be used to measure consistency for \emph{famillies} of POVM and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n\in \mathbb{N}$, which will always be clear from context but omitted for legibility, see Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}. The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}
   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}
   249	
   250	Note that a consistent measurement on $\ket{\psi}$ according to
   251	Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same $\ket{\psi}$ and under
   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]
   255	because using that $\{M_a\}$ is a POVM there must be equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
   256	\[ 1 = \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\, \leq\, \Big(\sum_a \|\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)\Big(\sum_a \|M_a\otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)^{1/2} \,\leq\,1 \;.\]
   257	
   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.
   271	\end{definition}

   185	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   186	      match W with
   187	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))

   189	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   190	      match W with
   191	      | .X => 0
   192	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   193	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   195	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   196	  | .inr _ => 0

   207	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   208	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   209	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   211	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   212	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,

   220	  | .aline _ => 2

   222	  | .pauli _ => 0
   223	  | .pairW _ => 1

   227	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   228	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   229	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   230	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,

   236	  match t with

   239	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   240	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   241	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   242	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   243	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection

   254	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   255	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   256	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   258	-/
   259	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   260	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   261	  let lineEdges :=
   262	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   263	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   264	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   265	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   266	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   267	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   268	  let basisEdges :=
   269	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   270	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   271	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   272	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   273	  let pairEdges :=
   274	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   275	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   276	  let msEdges' :=
   277	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   278	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   279	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   280	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   281	
   282	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   283	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   284	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   285	-/
   286	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   287	
   288	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   289	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   290	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   291	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   292	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   293	-/
   294	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   295	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   296	
   297	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   298	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   299	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   300	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   301	-/
   302	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   303	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   304	  simp [pauliEdges]
   305	
   306	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,
   307	then applying the endpoint CL maps.  This is the inlined typed-CL construction
   308	of `def:pauli-question-distribution` (blueprint lines 285-329; paper
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   311	noncomputable def pauliQuestionSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   312	    Finset (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   313	  by
   314	    classical
   315	    exact
   316	      (Finset.univ.filter fun s : (PauliType × PauliType) × PauliSpace P =>
   317	          Sym2.mk s.1.1 s.1.2 ∈ pauliEdges).image (fun s =>
   318	        ((s.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

   320	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   321	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   322	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   323	-/
   324	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   325	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   326	  by
   327	    classical
   328	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   329	    exact
   330	      Distribution.map
   331	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   332	        (fun s =>
   333	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   334	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

   336	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   337	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   338	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   339	-/
   340	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   341	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   342	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   343	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   344	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   345	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   346	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   347	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   348	  deriving DecidableEq

   350	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   351	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   352	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   353	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   354	-/
   355	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   356	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   357	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   358	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   359	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   360	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   361	
   362	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   363	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   364	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   365	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   366	-/
   367	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   368	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   369	  toFun
   370	    | .value a => .inl a
   371	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   372	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   373	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   374	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   375	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   376	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   377	  invFun
   378	    | .inl a => .value a
   379	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   380	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   381	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   382	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   383	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   384	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   385	  left_inv := by
   386	    intro x
   387	    cases x <;> rfl
   388	  right_inv := by
   389	    intro x
   390	    cases x with
   391	    | inl a => rfl
   392	    | inr x =>
   393	        cases x with
   394	        | inl a => rfl
   395	        | inr x =>
   396	            cases x with
   397	            | inl a => rfl
   398	            | inr x =>
   399	                cases x with
   400	                | inl a => rfl
   401	                | inr x =>
   402	                    cases x with
   403	                    | inl a => rfl
   404	                    | inr x =>
   405	                        cases x with
   406	                        | inl a => rfl
   407	                        | inr a => rfl

   409	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   410	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm

   412	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   413	  ⟨.bit 0⟩

   415	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   416	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   417	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   418	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   419	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   420	-/
   421	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   440	-/
   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   482	-/
   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      if tA = tB then
   534	        decide (a = b)
   535	      else
   536	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   537	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   538	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   539	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   540	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   541	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   542	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   543	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   544	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   545	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   546	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   547	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   548	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   549	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   550	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   551	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   552	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   553	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   554	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   555	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   556	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   557	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   563	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   564	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   565	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   566	          else true
   567	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   568	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   569	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   570	          else true
   571	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   572	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   573	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   574	          else true
   575	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   576	    else false

   578	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   579	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   580	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   581	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   582	-/
   583	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   584	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   585	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   586	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   587	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   588	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   589	  μ_prob := by sorry
   590	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

     7	/-!
     8	# The low-degree game
     9	
    10	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    11	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    12	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    13	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the low-degree game, including the fixed field model used by
    30	the ambient coefficient space.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:ld-game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    33	-/
    34	structure LdParams where
    35	  q : ℕ
    36	  m : ℕ
    37	  d : ℕ
    38	  k : ℕ
    39	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    40	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    41	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	  model : FixedFieldModel q
    45	
    46	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    47	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper
    48	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    49	-/
    50	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := P.model.K
    51	
    52	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    55	-/
    56	inductive LdType where
    57	  | point
    58	  | aline
    59	  | dline
    60	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    61	
    62	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    63	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    65	-/
    66	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    67	
    68	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    71	-/
    72	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    73	
    74	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    76	-/
    77	def LdSpace.point (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    78	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    79	
    80	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    82	-/
    83	def LdSpace.seed (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    84	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    85	
    86	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    88	-/
    89	def LdSpace.direction (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    90	  fun i => z (.inr i)
    91	
    92	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
    93	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    94	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
    98	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
    99	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   100	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   101	
   102	/-- The source uses the block quotient of the fixed integer representation.  The
   103	`Fin.ofNat` wrapper supplies the totalized boundary behavior for the temporary
   104	 skeleton's proof-irrelevant zero-dimension branch.  This is the projection
   105	 clause of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   106	 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   107	 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   108	-/
   109	def prefixProjection (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   110	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   111	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   112	
   113	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   114	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   117	-/
   118	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   119	  fun i => match i with
   120	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   121	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   122	  | .inr _ => 0
   123	
   124	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   125	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   126	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   127	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   128	-/
   129	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   130	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   131	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   132	  fun i => match i with
   133	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   134	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   135	  | .inr _ => 0
   136	
   137	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   138	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   139	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   140	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   141	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   142	-/
   143	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   144	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   145	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr j => direction j
   151	
   152	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   153	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   154	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   155	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   156	-/
   157	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   158	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   159	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   160	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   161	
   162	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   163	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   164	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   165	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   166	-/
   167	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   168	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   172	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   173	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   174	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   175	-/
   176	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   177	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   178	  sorry
   179	
   180	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   181	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   183	-/
   184	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   185	
   186	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   187	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
   188	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   189	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   190	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   191	-/
   192	noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
   193	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   194	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   195	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   196	
   197	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   198	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   199	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   202	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   203	  Distribution.map
   204	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   205	    (fun s =>
   206	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   207	
   208	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   209	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   210	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   211	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   212	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   213	-/
   214	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   215	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   218	  deriving DecidableEq
   219	
   220	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   221	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   222	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   223	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   224	-/
   225	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   226	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   228	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   229	
   230	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   231	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   232	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   233	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   234	-/
   235	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   236	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   237	  toFun
   238	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   239	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   240	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   241	  invFun
   242	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   243	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   244	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   245	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   246	  right_inv := by
   247	    intro x
   248	    cases x with
   249	    | inl a => rfl
   250	    | inr x =>
   251	        cases x with
   252	        | inl a => rfl
   253	        | inr a => rfl
   254	
   255	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   256	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   257	
   258	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   259	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   260	
   261	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   262	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   263	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   264	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   265	-/
   266	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   267	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   268	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   269	
   270	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   271	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   272	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   273	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   274	-/
   275	def validLdAnswer (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   276	  match t, a with
   277	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   278	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   279	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   280	  | _, _ => false
   281	
   282	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   283	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   284	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   285	-/
   286	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   287	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   288	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   289	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   290	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   291	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   292	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   293	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   294	
   295	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   296	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   297	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   298	-/
   299	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   300	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   301	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   307	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   308	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   310	-/
   311	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   312	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   313	  open Classical in
   314	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   315	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   316	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   317	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   318	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   319	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   320	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   321	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   322	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   328	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   329	      else false
   330	
   331	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   332	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   333	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   334	-/
   335	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   336	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   337	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   338	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   339	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   340	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   341	  μ_prob := by sorry
   342	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   343	
   344	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     7	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     8	
     9	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
    10	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
    11	`Measurement` structure.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    16	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    18	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/--
    29	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    30	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Game where
    35	  QuestionA : Type
    36	  QuestionB : Type
    37	  AnswerA : Type
    38	  AnswerB : Type
    39	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    40	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    41	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    42	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    43	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    44	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    45	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    46	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    47	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    48	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    49	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    50	
    51	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    52	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    53	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    54	
    55	/--
    56	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    57	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    58	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    59	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    61	-/
    62	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    63	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    64	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    65	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    66	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    67	
    68	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    69	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    70	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    71	-/
    72	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    73	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    74	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    75	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    76	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    77	
    78	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    79	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    81	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    82	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    83	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    84	
    85	/--
    86	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    87	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    88	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    89	-/
    90	structure Strategy (G : Game) where

    92	  ιB : Type

    95	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    96	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    97	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    98	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    99	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
   100	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
   101	
   102	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype

   104	
   105	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   106	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint

   108	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   109	-/
   110	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   111	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   112	
   113	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   114	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   115	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   116	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   117	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   119	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   120	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   121	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   122	
   123	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   124	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   126	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   127	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   128	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   129	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   130	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   131	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   132	
   133	/--
   134	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   135	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   136	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   137	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   138	-/
   139	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   140	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   141	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   142	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   143	
   144	/--
   145	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   146	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   147	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   148	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   149	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   150	intentionally not asserted here.
   151	-/
   152	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   153	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
