900	\label{sec:qld-game}
   901	
   902	We start by discussing parameter settings.
   903	The game $\game^\pauli$ is parametrized by a tuple
   904	\[\qldparams = (q,m,d)\;,\] where $q,m,d \in \N$ are integers. 
   905	We sometimes write $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
   906	Pauli basis test on the parameters.
   907	
   908	Informally, the test is meant to certify that the players share a state of the
   909	form $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}$, where $M=2^m$.
   910	Its question set includes questions that are axis-parallel/diagonal lines and points in $\F_q^m$,
   911	which are meant to correspond to questions in the classical low-degree test, and questions
   912	of the form $(\Pauli, W)$, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$.
   913	Upon receipt of a question of the latter form, the players are expected to
   914	perform the POVM $\{\tau_h^W\}_{h \in \F_q^{M}}$ and report the outcome $h$ as
   915	their answer.
   916	
   917	The key idea behind the test
   918	is for the provers to encode their outcomes using the \emph{low-degree encoding} from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
   919	Given an outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, the low-degree encoding of~$h$ is the polynomial $g_h:\F_q^m \rightarrow \F_q$.
   920	Rather than asking the provers to always return the entire string~$h$,
   921	many of the subtests in the game $\game^\pauli$ will ``probe'' limited information about~$h$ as follows:
   922	the verifier provides the provers with a string $u_W \in \F_q^m$,
   923	and using this they are expected to evaluate $g_h(u_W) \in \F_q$ and return it to the verifier.
   924	For a fixed value of~$W$, then, the prover's responses to these ``probes'' should be consistent with some low-degree polynomial in the input~$u_W$.
   925	To check this, the verifier can perform the classical low-degree test from Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}.
   926	This ensures that the prover's responses for the $W = X$ basis are consistent with each other,
   927	as well as their responses for the $W = Z$ basis, although it does not test consistency between the $X$ and $Z$ responses.
   928	
   929	The next set of subtests the verifier performs ensure that the provers' $X$ and $Z$ measurements are consistent with each other.
   930	On the $X$ side, consider the measurement in which the prover performs the $\{\tau_h^X\}$ POVM,
   931	receives outcome $h_X$, and outputs $g_{h_X}(u_X) \in \F_q$.
   932	For technical reasons that will become clear shortly,
   933	it will be convenient for the prover's measurement to have two outcomes rather than~$q$ outcomes.
   934	To accomplish this, the verifier also provides the prover with an element $r_X \in \F_q$;
   935	given this, the prover should output not $g_{h_X}(u_X) \in \F_q$ but $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$, which is an element of $\F_2$.
   936	Similarly, on the $Z$ side, suppose the prover is provided $r_Z \in \F_q$,
   937	performs $\{\tau_h^Z\}$ to receive $h_Z$, and outputs $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z) \in \F_2$.
   938	Together, these two are a pair of two-outcome measurements, one in the~$X$ basis and one in the~$Z$ basis,
   939	and as it turns out, this pair of measurements either commutes with each other or anticommutes with each other
   940	(this is why we modified the measurements to have only two outcomes).
   941	The key quantity to determine which of these is the case is the following complicated-looking expression:
   942	\begin{equation*}
   943	\gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
   944	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;.
   945	\end{equation*}
   946	If $\gamma = 0$, then these two measurements commute, and if $\gamma = 1$, then these two measurements anticommute
   947	(this fact is established in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness} below).
   948	In the $\gamma = 0$ case, the verifier can check whether these two measurements commute by performing the ``commutation check'',
   949	which asks the provers to simultaneously measure both $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$ and $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z)$ and report their values.
   950	In the $\gamma = 1$ case, on the other hand, the measurements anticommute, which implies that they cannot simultaneously be measured.
   951	In spite of this, the verifier can still check that the measurements anticommute by using the Magic Square game from Section~\ref{sec:ms} above.
   952	As was shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, any pair of anticommuting measurements
   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game
   954	(and indeed the reverse is true as well: any perfect strategy for the Magic Square game entails a pair of anticommuting measurements).
   955	
   956	Together, these give the main subtests for the game $\game^\pauli$.
   957	
   958	\begin{definition}[Admissible parameters]\label{def:admissible}
   959	  We say that the tuple $\qldparams=(q, m, d)$ is \emph{admissible} if $q$ is
   960	  an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m | q$.
   961	\end{definition}
   962	
   963	
   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.
   975	
   976	
   977	
   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.
  1009		\end{enumerate}
  1010	\end{enumerate}

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114

  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where

  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

  1188	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).

  1190	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\Pauli, W)$, accept if
  1191	      $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}(x_w) = a_w$, where $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}$ is
  1192	      the low-degree encoding of $a_{\overline{w}} \in \F_q^M$ defined in
  1193	      Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1194	    \end{enumerate}
  1195	    In the remaining four cases, the decision procedure first computes the
  1196	    number
  1197	    \begin{equation}
  1198	      \label{eq:gamma-value}
  1199	      \gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
  1200	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;,
  1201	    \end{equation}
  1202	    where we recall the $\ind_{m}(\cdot)$ vector from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1203	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1204	      \setcounter{enumi}{3}
  1205	    \item (\textbf{Commutation check}).
  1206	      \label{item:commutation} If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1207	      \Pair$, accept if $a_w = \beta_W$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1208	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1209	      \label{item:commutation-consistency} If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1210	      (\Pair,W)$, accept if $\tr (a_w r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1211	      
  1212	    \item (\textbf{Magic square check}).
  1213	      \label{item:magic-square} If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i,
  1214	      \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if $\gamma = 0$, or $a_w$
  1215	      satisfies constraint $\Constraint_i$ and $ \alpha_j = a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1216	
  1217	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1218	      \label{item:magic-square-consistency}
  1219	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if
  1220	      $\gamma = 0$ or if $j = 1$, $W = X$, and $\tr(a_w r_\xpt) =
  1221	      a_{\overline{w}}$ or if $j = 5$, $W = Z$, and $\tr(a_w r_\zpt) =
  1222	      a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1223	    \end{enumerate}
  1224	  \end{gamespec}
  1225	  \caption{Specification of the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli_\qldparams$.}
  1226	  \label{fig:decider_pauli}

  1229	We describe an honest, value-$1$ PCC strategy for the Pauli basis test.

  1232	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pauli-completeness}
  1233	  The Pauli basis test $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ has a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.

     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     7	
     8	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     9	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
    10	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    11	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    16	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    28	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    29	
    30	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    31	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    33	-/
    34	inductive PauliKind where
    35	  | X
    36	  | Z
    37	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    38	
    39	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    40	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    41	
    42	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    43	character in their statement types. -/
    44	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    45	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    46	
    47	/--
    48	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    49	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    51	-/
    52	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    53	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    54	
    55	/--
    56	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    57	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    61	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    62	
    63	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    64	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    65	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    66	  match W with
    67	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    68	  | .X =>
    69	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    70	
    71	/--
    72	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    73	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    74	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    75	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    77	-/
    78	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    79	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    80	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    81	
    82	/--
    83	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    84	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    85	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    86	-/
    87	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    88	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    89	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    90	
    91	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    92	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    93	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    94	-/
    95	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    96	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    97	  fun x y =>
    98	    ∏ i : ι,
    99	      match W with
   100	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   102	
   103	/--
   104	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   109	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   110	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   111	    (fun p : V × V =>
   112	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   113	
   114	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   115	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/

   117	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   118	  sorry

   126	-/
   127	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   128	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   129	    tauObservable W a =
   130	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   131	  sorry
   132	
   133	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   134	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   135	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   136	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   137	-/

   142	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by

     3	/-!

     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.

    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,

    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.

    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution
   101	
   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm
   117	
   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   127	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.
   128	
   129	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   130	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   131	than over a stored support finset. -/
   132	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   133	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   134	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   135	  rw [Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟 𝒟.weight 𝒟.outsideSupport]
   136	  exact h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   137	
   138	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   139	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   140	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   141	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   142	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   143	
   144	/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
   145	theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   146	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   147	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
   148	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟
   149	
   150	end Distribution.IsProbability
   151	
   152	namespace Distribution
   153	
   154	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
   155	whose total mass is one.
   156	
   157	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
   158	`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
   159	probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
   160	noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   161	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
   162	  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
   163	    (by
   164	      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
   165	        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
   166	      simp)
   167	    (by
   168	      intro a ha
   169	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   170	      simp)
   171	
   172	@[simp]
   173	theorem toPMF_apply {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   174	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   175	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a) := rfl
   176	
   177	@[simp]
   178	theorem toPMF_apply_toReal {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   179	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   180	    (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal = 𝒟.weight a := by
   181	  rw [toPMF_apply, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   182	
   183	/-- The associated PMF has zero mass outside the stored support of the project
   184	distribution. -/
   185	theorem toPMF_apply_of_notMem {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   186	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {a : α} (ha : a ∉ 𝒟.support) :
   187	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = 0 := by
   188	  rw [toPMF_apply, 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   189	  simp
   190	
   191	/-- The project push-forward agrees with Mathlib's push-forward of the
   192	associated probability mass function. -/
   193	theorem toPMF_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   194	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   195	    (𝒟.map e).toPMF (h𝒟.map e) = (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).map e := by
   196	  classical
   197	  ext b
   198	  rw [toPMF_apply, PMF.map_apply, map_weight]
   199	  rw [ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg
   200	    (s := 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b))
   201	    (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   202	  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := 𝒟.support)]
   203	  · rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   204	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   205	    intro a ha
   206	    by_cases hea : e a = b
   207	    · have hba : b = e a := hea.symm
   208	      rw [if_pos hea, if_pos hba, toPMF_apply]
   209	    · have hba : b ≠ e a := fun hba => hea hba.symm
   210	      rw [if_neg hea, if_neg hba]
   211	  · intro a ha
   212	    by_cases hba : b = e a
   213	    · rw [if_pos hba, toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
   214	    · rw [if_neg hba]
   215	
   216	end Distribution

   218	/-- Average a scalar function against the stored finite support of a distribution. -/
   219	def avgOver {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) : Error :=
   220	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a
   221	
   222	namespace Distribution
   223	
   224	/-- The module-valued weighted finite sum associated to a finite-support `Distribution`,
   225	as a linear map in the averaged family.
   226	
   227	This packages the finite-support expression underlying both scalar averages and
   228	operator averages.  It keeps the explicit support carried by `Distribution`,
   229	while exposing the `Error`-module structure of the weighted sum. -/
   230	noncomputable def weightedSumLinearMap (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
   231	    {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : (α → M) →ₗ[Error] M where
   232	  toFun := fun f => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a
   233	  map_add' := fun f g => by
   234	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   235	  map_smul' := fun c f => by
   236	    simp only [Pi.smul_apply]
   237	    calc
   238	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • c • f a =
   239	          ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, c • (𝒟.weight a • f a) := by
   240	            refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   241	            intro a _
   242	            rw [smul_smul, smul_smul, mul_comm]
   243	      _ = c • ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a := by
   244	            rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   245	
   246	@[simp]
   247	theorem weightedSumLinearMap_apply (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
   248	    {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → M) :
   249	    𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap M f = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a :=
   250	  rfl
   251	
   252	/-- The scalar average is the weighted finite-sum linear map applied to a scalar
   253	family. -/
   254	theorem avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap {α : Type*}
   255	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) :
   256	    avgOver 𝒟 f = 𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error f := by
   257	  simp [avgOver, smul_eq_mul]
   258	
   259	/-- Averaging against a pushed-forward distribution is averaging the pulled-back
   260	function against the original distribution. -/
   261	theorem avgOver_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   262	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → Error) :
   263	    avgOver (𝒟.map e) f = avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f (e a)) := by
   264	  simpa [avgOver, smul_eq_mul] using
   265	    Distribution.map_sum_smul (𝒟 := 𝒟) e f
   266	
   267	end Distribution
   268	
   269	/-- Weighted sum of operators over a distribution's finite support, using the same
   270	`support`/`weight` data as the scalar `avgOver`.
   271	
   272	This is a project-local adapter around Mathlib finite sums for the LDT
   273	`Distribution` representation and `Quantum.Op` scalar action, not a replacement for
   274	Mathlib's probability theory APIs. -/
   275	noncomputable def averageOperatorOverDistribution {α : Type*}
   276	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   277	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
   278	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a
   279	
   280	namespace Distribution
   281	
   282	/-- Operator averaging is the weighted finite-sum linear map applied to an
   283	operator-valued family. -/
   284	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_eq_weightedSumLinearMap {α : Type*}
   285	    (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   286	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   287	    (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   288	    averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 f =
   289	      𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap (MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) f :=
   290	  rfl
   291	
   292	/-- Operator-valued averaging against a pushed-forward distribution is
   293	operator-valued averaging of the pulled-back family against the original
   294	distribution. -/
   295	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   296	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β)
   297	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   298	    (f : β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   299	    averageOperatorOverDistribution (𝒟.map e) f =
   300	      averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => f (e a)) := by
   301	  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
   302	    Distribution.map_sum_smul (𝒟 := 𝒟) e f
   303	
   304	end Distribution
   305	
   306	/-- If two operator-valued families agree pointwise, their averages agree. -/
   307	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_congr {α : Type*}
   308	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   309	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (A B : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)
   310	    (h : ∀ a, A a = B a) :
   311	    averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A = averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 B := by
   312	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by rw [h a]

     8	
     9	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite

    12	needed by later formalization stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    17	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
    18	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
    19	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.

    22	open scoped BigOperators

    27	
    28	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    32	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    33	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    34	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    35	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    36	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    37	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    38	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    39	-/
    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    49	
    50	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    51	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    52	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    59	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    61	-/
    62	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    63	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    64	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    65	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    66	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    67	      fun x =>
    68	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    69	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    70	
    71	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    72	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    73	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    74	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    75	-/
    76	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    78	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    79	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    80	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    81	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    82	
    83	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    84	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    87	-/
    88	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    89	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    90	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    91	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    92	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    93	
    94	/--
    95	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    96	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    98	-/
    99	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   100	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   104	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   109	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   110	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   111	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   112	
   113	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   114	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   115	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   116	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   117	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   119	-/
   120	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   121	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   122	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   123	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   124	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   125	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   126	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   127	
   128	/--
   129	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is

   131	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   132	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the
   133	level proof remains deferred in this skeleton.
   134	-/
   135	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   136	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   137	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   138	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}

   142	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)

   146	/--

   151	The underlying graph-distribution definition is

   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   155	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=

   158

     3	/-!
     4	# Basic finite-dimensional matrix operators
     5	
     6	This module contains the elementary trace and matrix-algebra facts used by the
     7	finite-dimensional quantum layer.  It introduces the local operator abbreviation
     8	`Op d = Matrix d d ℂ` and keeps the basic trace bookkeeping independent of the
     9	positive-semidefinite order and normalized-trace material.

    18	open WithLp
    19	
    20	namespace Matrix
    21	
    22	/-! ### Trace bookkeeping -/
    23	
    24	/-- Reindexing rows and columns by the same equivalence preserves matrix trace.
    25	
    26	This generic matrix lemma is used when moving between equivalent finite index
    27	presentations of the same operator. -/
    28	theorem trace_reindex {α β R : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    29	    [AddCommMonoid R] (e : α ≃ β) (M : Matrix α α R) :
    30	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.reindex e e M) = Matrix.trace M := by
    31	  classical
    32	  simp only [Matrix.trace, Matrix.diag_apply, Matrix.reindex_apply]
    33	  rw [← e.symm.sum_comp (fun i : α => M i i)]
    34	  rfl
    35	
    36	/-! ### Linear matrix maps -/
    37	
    38	/-- Taking a submatrix is linear in the ambient matrix.
    39	
    40	This packages the entrywise linearity of `Matrix.submatrix` in the same style
    41	as Mathlib's block-diagonal additive and linear maps. -/
    42	def submatrixLinearMap (R : Type*) {m n m' n' α : Type*}
    43	    [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    44	    (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) :
    45	    Matrix m n α →ₗ[R] Matrix m' n' α where
    46	  toFun := fun A => Matrix.submatrix A row col
    47	  map_add' := by
    48	    intro A B
    49	    ext i j
    50	    rfl
    51	  map_smul' := by
    52	    intro c A
    53	    ext i j
    54	    rfl
    55	
    56	@[simp]
    57	theorem submatrixLinearMap_apply (R : Type*) {m n m' n' α : Type*}
    58	    [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    59	    (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) (A : Matrix m n α) :
    60	    Matrix.submatrixLinearMap R row col A = Matrix.submatrix A row col :=
    61	  rfl
    62	
    63	/-- The trace pairing of two block-diagonal matrices is the sum of the trace
    64	pairings of the corresponding diagonal blocks. -/
    65	theorem trace_blockDiagonal_mul {o m R : Type*}
    66	    [Fintype o] [DecidableEq o] [Fintype m] [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring R]
    67	    (B D : o → Matrix m m R) :
    68	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.blockDiagonal B * Matrix.blockDiagonal D) =
    69	      ∑ b : o, Matrix.trace (B b * D b) := by
    70	  rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul B D, Matrix.trace_blockDiagonal]
    71	
    72	end Matrix

    75	
    76	/-! ### Basic operator type -/
    77	
    78	/-- Square complex matrices as the finite-dimensional operator algebra. -/
    79	abbrev Op (d : Type*) := Matrix d d ℂ
    80	
    81	/-! ### Kronecker product bookkeeping -/
    82	
    83	/-- Kronecker product is additive in the right factor, rewritten for subtraction. -/
    84	theorem kronecker_sub_right
    85	    {d₁ d₂ : Type*} {A : Op d₁} {B₁ B₂ : Op d₂} :
    86	    Matrix.kronecker A B₁ - Matrix.kronecker A B₂ =
    87	      Matrix.kronecker A (B₁ - B₂) := by
    88	  have hneg : Matrix.kronecker A (-B₂) = -Matrix.kronecker A B₂ := by
    89	    simpa using (Matrix.kronecker_smul (-1 : ℂ) A B₂)
    90	  calc
    91	    Matrix.kronecker A B₁ - Matrix.kronecker A B₂
    92	        = Matrix.kronecker A B₁ + Matrix.kronecker A (-B₂) := by
    93	            rw [hneg]
    94	            simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
    95	    _ = Matrix.kronecker A (B₁ - B₂) := by
    96	          simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using (Matrix.kronecker_add A B₁ (-B₂)).symm
    97	
    98	/-- Kronecker product is additive in the left factor, rewritten for subtraction. -/
    99	theorem kronecker_sub_left
   100	    {d₁ d₂ : Type*} {A₁ A₂ : Op d₁} {B : Op d₂} :
   101	    Matrix.kronecker A₁ B - Matrix.kronecker A₂ B =
   102	      Matrix.kronecker (A₁ - A₂) B := by
   103	  have hneg : Matrix.kronecker (-A₂) B = -Matrix.kronecker A₂ B := by
   104	    simpa using (Matrix.smul_kronecker (-1 : ℂ) A₂ B)
   105	  calc
   106	    Matrix.kronecker A₁ B - Matrix.kronecker A₂ B
   107	        = Matrix.kronecker A₁ B + Matrix.kronecker (-A₂) B := by
   108	            rw [hneg]
   109	            simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
   110	    _ = Matrix.kronecker (A₁ - A₂) B := by
   111	          simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using (Matrix.add_kronecker A₁ (-A₂) B).symm
   112	
   113	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

1	\section{Conditionally Linear Functions, Distributions, and Samplers}
     2	\label{sec:linear}
     3	
     4	\subsection{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}
     5	\label{sec:cl}
     6	
     7	We first introduce \emph{conditionally linear functions}, which are used to
     8	specify the question distribution for games considered in the paper in a way
     9	that the question distribution can be ``introspected'', as described in
    10	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}.
    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}
    86	
    87	\begin{figure}[!htbp]
    88	  \centering
    89	  \begin{tikzpicture}
    90	
    91	
    92	
    93	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=east] at (0,0) (xv1) {$x^{V_{1}}$};
    94	    \node[draw, minimum width=6cm, anchor=west] at (-.4pt,0) {$x^{V_{>1}}$};
    95	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=east] at (0,-2) (xl1) {$x^{L_{1}}$};
    96	    \draw[-stealth] (xv1.south) -- ++(0,-1) node[above right] {$L_{1}$} -- (xl1.north);
    97	
    98	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-3) (xv2) {$x^{V_{2}}$};
    99	    \node[draw, minimum width=4cm, anchor=west] at (2cm,-3) {$x^{V_{>2}}$};
   100	
   101	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-5) (xl2) {$x^{L_{2}}$};
   102	
   103	    \draw[-stealth] (xv2.south) -- ++(0,-1) node[above right]
   104	      {$L_{2,\,x^{{L_{1}}}}$} -- (xl2.north);

   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};

   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called

   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.

   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}

   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.

   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.

   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,

   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.

   960	  an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m | q$.
   961	\end{definition}

   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.
   975	
   976	
   977	
   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.
  1009		\end{enumerate}
  1010	\end{enumerate}

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

  1128	Figure~\ref{fig:decider_pauli}.

  1131	The answers are bit strings that are interpreted as more structured objects such
  1132	as elements over $\F_q$, vectors, or polynomials, depending on the question.
  1133	In the ``low-degree check'', the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ calls the
  1134	classical low-degree decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ parametrized by the tuple

  1169	    On input $(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice, \tvar_\bob, x_\bob, a_\alice, a_\bob)$,
  1170	    the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ performs the following checks for
  1171	    $w \in \AB$:
  1172	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1173	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1174	      \label{item:same-type}
  1175	      If $\tvar_\alice = \tvar_\bob$, accept iff $a_\alice = a_\bob$.
  1176	
  1177	    \item (\textbf{Low-degree}).
  1178	      \label{item:low-degree}
  1179	      Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,1)$. 
  1180	      \begin{enumerate}
  1181	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\ALine, W)$, accept if
  1182	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \ALine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1183	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1184	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\DLine, W)$, accept if
  1185	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \DLine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1186	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1187			\end{enumerate}
  1188	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1189	      \label{item:low-degree-consistency}
  1190	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\Pauli, W)$, accept if
  1191	      $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}(x_w) = a_w$, where $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}$ is
  1192	      the low-degree encoding of $a_{\overline{w}} \in \F_q^M$ defined in
  1193	      Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1194	    \end{enumerate}
  1195	    In the remaining four cases, the decision procedure first computes the
  1196	    number
  1197	    \begin{equation}
  1198	      \label{eq:gamma-value}
  1199	      \gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
  1200	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;,
  1201	    \end{equation}
  1202	    where we recall the $\ind_{m}(\cdot)$ vector from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1203	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1204	      \setcounter{enumi}{3}
  1205	    \item (\textbf{Commutation check}).
  1206	      \label{item:commutation} If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1207	      \Pair$, accept if $a_w = \beta_W$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1208	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1209	      \label{item:commutation-consistency} If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1210	      (\Pair,W)$, accept if $\tr (a_w r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1211	      
  1212	    \item (\textbf{Magic square check}).
  1213	      \label{item:magic-square} If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i,
  1214	      \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if $\gamma = 0$, or $a_w$
  1215	      satisfies constraint $\Constraint_i$ and $ \alpha_j = a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1216	
  1217	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1218	      \label{item:magic-square-consistency}
  1219	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if
  1220	      $\gamma = 0$ or if $j = 1$, $W = X$, and $\tr(a_w r_\xpt) =
  1221	      a_{\overline{w}}$ or if $j = 5$, $W = Z$, and $\tr(a_w r_\zpt) =
  1222	      a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1223	    \end{enumerate}

   409	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=

   415	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   416	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   417	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   418	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   419	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.

   421	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      if tA = tB then
   534	        decide (a = b)
   535	      else
   536	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   537	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   538	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   539	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   540	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   541	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   542	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   543	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   544	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   545	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   546	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   547	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   548	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   549	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   550	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   551	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   552	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   553	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   554	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   555	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   556	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   557	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   563	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   564	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   565	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   566	          else true
   567	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   568	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   569	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   570	          else true
   571	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   572	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   573	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   574	          else true
   575	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   576	    else false
   577	
   578	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   579	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   580	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   581	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   582	-/
   583	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   584	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   585	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   586	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   587	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   588	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   589	  μ_prob := by sorry
   590	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   591	
   592	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex-107-\begin{remark}[Diagonal questions with zero direction]\label{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:108:	The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex-109-\end{remark}
