     7	/-!
     8	# The low-degree game
     9	
    10	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    11	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    12	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    13	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the low-degree game, including the fixed field model used by
    30	the ambient coefficient space.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:ld-game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    33	-/
    34	structure LdParams where
    35	  q : ℕ
    36	  m : ℕ
    37	  d : ℕ
    38	  k : ℕ
    39	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    40	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    41	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	  model : FixedFieldModel q
    45	
    46	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    47	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper
    48	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    49	-/
    50	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := P.model.K
    51	
    52	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    55	-/
    56	inductive LdType where
    57	  | point
    58	  | aline
    59	  | dline
    60	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    61	
    62	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    63	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    65	-/
    66	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    67	
    68	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    71	-/
    72	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    73	
    74	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    76	-/
    77	def LdSpace.point (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    78	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    79	
    80	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    82	-/
    83	def LdSpace.seed (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    84	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    85	
    86	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    88	-/
    89	def LdSpace.direction (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    90	  fun i => z (.inr i)
    91	
    92	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
    93	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    94	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
    98	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
    99	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   100	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   101	
   102	/-- The source uses the block quotient of the fixed integer representation.  The
   103	`Fin.ofNat` wrapper supplies the totalized boundary behavior for the temporary
   104	 skeleton's proof-irrelevant zero-dimension branch.  This is the projection
   105	 clause of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   106	 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   107	 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   108	-/
   109	def prefixProjection (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   110	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   111	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   112	
   113	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   114	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   117	-/
   118	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   119	  fun i => match i with
   120	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   121	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   122	  | .inr _ => 0
   123	
   124	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   125	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   126	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   127	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   128	-/
   129	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   130	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   131	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   132	  fun i => match i with
   133	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   134	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   135	  | .inr _ => 0
   136	
   137	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   138	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   139	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   140	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   141	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   142	-/
   143	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   144	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   145	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr j => direction j
   151	
   152	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   153	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   154	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   155	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   156	-/
   157	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   158	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   159	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   160	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   161	
   162	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   163	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   164	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   165	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   166	-/
   167	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   168	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   172	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   173	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   174	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   175	-/
   176	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   177	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   178	  sorry
   179	
   180	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   181	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   183	-/
   184	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   185	
   186	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   187	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
   188	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   189	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   190	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   191	-/
   192	noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
   193	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   194	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   195	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   196	
   197	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   198	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   199	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   202	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   203	  Distribution.map
   204	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   205	    (fun s =>
   206	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   207	
   208	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   209	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   210	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   211	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   212	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   213	-/
   214	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   215	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    76	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    78	-/
    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80	
    81	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97	
    98	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   100	
   101	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   102	
   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   122	
   123	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate
   135	
   136	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    62	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm

186:We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
188:\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
190:	The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.

267:The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

    24	\begin{definition}[Register subspace]\label{def:register-subspace}
    25		A \emph{register subspace} $S$ of $V$ is a subspace that is the span of a
    26		subset of the standard basis of $V$. Such a subspace is represented by an
    27		indicator vector $u \in \{0,1\}^s$, where $s = \dim(V)$, via
    28		$S = \mathrm{span}\{\hat{e}_i : u_i = 1\}$.
    29	\end{definition}

    31	\begin{definition}[Dot product and orthogonal subspace]\label{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    32		For two vectors $u = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \hat{e}_i$ and
    33		$v = \sum_{i=1}^n v_i \hat{e}_i$ in $V = \F^n$, the \emph{dot product} is
    34		\[
    35			u \cdot v = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i v_i \in \F\;.
    36		\]
    37		For a subspace $S$ of $V$, the \emph{subspace orthogonal to $S$ in $V$} is
    38		\[
    39			S^\perp = \bigl\{ u \in V : u \cdot v = 0 \text{ for all } v \in S \bigr\}\;.
    40		\]
    41		The notation $S^\perp$ leaves the ambient space $V$ implicit.
    42	\end{definition}
    43	
    44	Over finite fields, orthogonality lacks some of the familiar properties it has
    45	over $\R$ or $\C$; for example, a nonzero subspace may be orthogonal to itself,
    46	as is $\mathrm{span}\{(1,1)\}$ over $\F_2$. The following dimension identity
    47	nevertheless holds over every field.
    48	
    49	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:perp_perp}
    50		\uses{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    51		Let $S$ be a subspace of $V$. Then $\dim(S) + \dim(S^\perp) = \dim(V)$, and
    52		\[
    53			(S^\perp)^\perp = S\;.
    54		\]
    55	\end{lemma}
    56	\begin{proof}
    57		\uses{def:dot-product-orthogonal}
    58		The elements of $S^\perp$ are the solutions of a feasible linear system whose
    59		coefficient matrix has $\dim(S)$ linearly independent rows, so the solution
    60		space has dimension exactly $\dim(V) - \dim(S)$. Every $u \in S$ is
    61		orthogonal to every element of $S^\perp$, so $S \subseteq (S^\perp)^\perp$.
    62		Applying the dimension identity twice shows that
    63		$\dim\bigl((S^\perp)^\perp\bigr) = \dim(S)$, so the inclusion is an equality.
    64	\end{proof}

    66	\begin{definition}[Complementary subspaces]\label{def:complementary}
    67		Two subspaces $S$ and $T$ of a linear space $V$ form a pair of
    68		\emph{complementary subspaces} of $V$ if
    69		\[
    70			S \cap T = \{0\}\;, \qquad S + T = V\;.
    71		\]
    72		In this case we write $V = S \oplus T$. Every $x \in V$ can be written
    73		uniquely as $x = x^S + x^T$ with $x^S \in S$ and $x^T \in T$; we call $x^S$
    74		(resp.\ $x^T$) the \emph{projection of $x$ onto $S$ parallel to $T$} (resp.\
    75		onto $T$ parallel to $S$). The unique linear map $L : V \to V$ with
    76		$x \mapsto x^S$ is the \emph{projector onto $S$ parallel to $T$}.
    77	\end{definition}

    81	$\mathrm{span}\{(1,0)\}$ and $\mathrm{span}\{(0,1)\}$. Given a basis of $S$,

    84	\begin{definition}[Canonical complement]\label{def:canonical-complement}

    86		Let $\hat{E}$ be the standard basis of $V = \F^n$ and let

    88		vectors. Write $v_i = \sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,j}\, \hat{e}_j$, and, using a
    89		canonical Gaussian-elimination algorithm valid over arbitrary fields,
    90		transform the $m \times n$ matrix $(a_{i,j})$ to reduced row echelon form
    91		$(b_{i,j})$. Let $J$ be the set of $m$ column indices containing the leading
    92		$1$ entry of each row of $(b_{i,j})$. The \emph{canonical complement of $F$}
    93		is the set of $n - m$ standard basis vectors
    94		\[
    95			F^\perp = \{\hat{e}_j : j \notin J\}\;.
    96		\]

   112	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:canonical-complement}
   113		\uses{def:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   114		Let $S$ be the span of linearly independent vectors
   115		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subseteq V$, let $F^\perp$ be the canonical
   116		complement of $F$, and let $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$. Then

   124		write $A = UB$ with $U$ invertible and $B$ in reduced row echelon form, so

   133	\begin{definition}[Canonical linear map with prescribed kernel]\label{def:cl-canonical}
   134		\uses{def:canonical-complement, lem:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   135		Let $F \subseteq V$ be a set of linearly independent vectors and let
   136		$F^\perp$ be its canonical complement. The \emph{canonical linear map
   137		$L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ with kernel basis $F$} is the projector onto $T$
   138		parallel to $S$, where $S = \mathrm{span}(F)$ and
   139		$T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$; this is well defined by
   140		Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-complement}. Since the canonical complement
   141		depends only on $\mathrm{span}(F)$
   142		(Definition~\ref{def:canonical-complement}), so does $L$, and we also call
   143		it the \emph{canonical linear map with kernel $S$}. Note that
   144		$\ker(L) = S$.
   145	\end{definition}
   146	
   147	\begin{definition}[The map $L^\perp$]\label{def:Lperp}
   148		\uses{def:cl-canonical, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   149		Let $L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ be a linear map and let $F$ be a basis for
   150		$\ker(L)^\perp$. Define $L^\perp : V \to V$ as the canonical linear map with
   151		kernel basis $F$. (By the basis-independence noted in
   152		Definition~\ref{def:canonical-complement}, the map $L^\perp$ depends only
   153		on $\ker(L)$ and not on the chosen basis $F$.)
   154	\end{definition}
   155	
   156	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L_perp_perp}
   157		\uses{def:Lperp}
   158		Let $L \in \mathrm{End}(V)$ be a linear map, $F$ a basis for
   159		$\ker(L)^\perp$, and $L^\perp$ as in Definition~\ref{def:Lperp}. Then
   160		$\ker(L^\perp) = \ker(L)^\perp$.
   161	\end{lemma}
   162	\begin{proof}
   163		\uses{def:Lperp, def:cl-canonical, lem:canonical-complement}
   164		Set $S = \mathrm{span}(F) = \ker(L)^\perp$ and $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$;
   165		by Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-complement} every $v \in V$ decomposes uniquely
   166		as $v = v^S + v^T$, and by definition $L^\perp v = v^T$. If
   167		$L^\perp v = 0$ then $v = v^S \in S = \ker(L)^\perp$. Conversely, if
   168		$v \in S$ then $v^T = 0$, so $L^\perp v = 0$.
   169	\end{proof}

   178	Let $p$ be a prime and $q = p^k$ a prime power. We write $\F_p$ and $\F_q$ for
   179	the finite fields with $p$ and $q$ elements; $p$ is the characteristic of
   180	$\F_q$, and $\F_p$ is its prime subfield.

320	
   321	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree]\label{def:polynomials-degree}
   322		\uses{def:polyfunc}
   323		An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   324		\[
   325			f(x_1, \dots, x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m}
   326			c_\alpha\, x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   327		\]
   328		with coefficients $c_\alpha \in \F_q$; the coefficients are uniquely
   329		determined by $f$, since the $q^m$ monomial functions indexed by
   330		$\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m$ span the $q^m$-dimensional space of all
   331		functions $\F_q^m \to \F_q$ and are therefore linearly independent. The
   332		polynomial $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if
   333		$c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when $\alpha_i \le d$ for all $1 \le i \le m$, and
   334		\emph{total degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when
   335		$\sum_i \alpha_i \le d$. (Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are those
   336		of individual degree $1$.
   337		% Relationship to def:polyfunc: polyfunc keeps polynomial representatives,
   338		% so evaluation identifies it with the function classes above only for
   339		% d <= q-1.
   340		Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc} introduces the set $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ of
   341		polynomials in $\F_q[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ of degree at most $d$ in each
   342		variable, identified by their polynomial representatives rather than by the
   343		functions they induce. Evaluation maps $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ onto the set of
   344		$m$-variate polynomials of individual degree at most $\min(d, q-1)$ in the
   345		sense above; for $d \le q-1$ this map is a bijection, while for $d \ge q$
   346		distinct representatives, such as $x_1^q$ and $x_1$, induce the same
   347		function. Statements phrased in terms of $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ retain the
   348		representative convention of Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}.
   349	\end{definition}
   350	
   351	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz--Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]\label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   352		% Restatement of lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree under the source's label.
   353		\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
   354		Let $f, g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials of total degree at
   355		most $d$. Then
   356		\[
   357			\Prb_{\bx \sim \F_q^m}[f(\bx) = g(\bx)] \le \frac{d}{q}\;.
   358		\]
   359	\end{lemma}
   360	\begin{proof}
   361		\uses{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   362		This is Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}, stated and proved in
   363		Chapter~\ref{chap:preliminaries}; it is restated here under the label used
   364		by \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   365	\end{proof}
   366	
   367	\begin{remark}\label{rem:schwartz-zippel-restated}
   368		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel} restates the total-degree bound of
   369		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} under the label used by
   370		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The individual-degree consequence,
   371		Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-individual}, shows that distinct elements of
   372		$\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ agree on at most an $md/q$ fraction of the points of
   373		$\F_q^m$; the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses the bound in this
   374		individual-degree form.
   375	\end{remark}
   376	
   377	The Schwartz--Zippel lemma implies that low-degree polynomials form an
   378	error-correcting code with good distance, the \emph{low-degree code} (a special
   379	case of the generalized Reed--Muller code).
   380	
   381	\begin{definition}[Low-degree encoding]\label{def:low-degree-encoding}
   382		\uses{def:polynomials-degree}
   383		Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$. For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   384		define the $m$-variate multilinear polynomial over $\F_q$
   385		\[
   386			\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)
   387			= \prod_{i : y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i : y_i = 0} (1 - x_i)\;,
   388		\]
   389		identifying $\{0,1\}$ with a subset of $\F_q$. Restricted to the subcube
   390		$\{0,1\}^m$, the polynomial $\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}$ vanishes everywhere except
   391		at $x = y$, where it equals $1$. For $a \in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates
   392		of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ (identifying $\{0,1\}^m$ with
   393		$\{1, \dots, M\}$ by the lexicographic ordering). The \emph{low-degree
   394		encoding of $a$} is the multilinear polynomial $g_a : \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   395		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   396		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   397			g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\;.
   398		\end{equation}
   399		For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ one has $g_a(y) = a_y$, and $g_a$ has total
   400		degree at most $m$.
   401	\end{definition}
   402	
   403	\begin{definition}[Indicator vector and linearity of the encoding]\label{def:indicator-vector}
   404		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   405		For $x \in \F_q^m$, the \emph{indicator vector} is
   406		\[
   407			\mathrm{ind}_m(x)
   408			= \bigl(\mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(x)\bigr)_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \in \F_q^M\;.
   409		\]
   410		With this notation the low-degree encoding satisfies, for every
   411		$a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$,
   412		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   413		\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   414			g_a(x) = a \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)\;;
   415		\end{equation}
   416		in particular the map $a \mapsto g_a$ is $\F_q$-linear.
   417	\end{definition}
   418	
   419	Since encodings $g_a$ are multilinear, hence of total degree at most $m$, two
   420	encodings of distinct strings agree on at most an $m/q$ fraction of points of
   421	$\F_q^m$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel}.
   422	
   423	\begin{definition}[Decoding maps]\label{def:decoding-map}
   424		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding}
   425		For $H \subseteq \F_q$, the \emph{decoding map} $\mathrm{Dec}_H$ takes as
   426		input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and returns the vector
   427		$a \in \F_q^M$ defined by: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, set $a_y = g(y)$ if
   428		$g(y) \in H$, and $a_y = 0$ otherwise. For all $a \in H^M$ one has
   429		$\mathrm{Dec}_H(g_a) = a$. We write $\mathrm{Dec}(\cdot)$ for the boolean
   430		decoding map $\mathrm{Dec}_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.
   431	\end{definition}

   433	\section{Lines}
   434	
   435	The question distributions of the classical low individual degree game and of
   436	the Pauli basis test (Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}) sample lines in $\F_q^m$;
   437	we record here the definition of lines and their canonical representatives.
   438	
   439	\begin{definition}[Lines]\label{def:line}
   440		A \emph{line} $\ell$ in $\F_q^m$ specified by a pair
   441		$(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$ is the subset
   442		\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-set}
   443			\ell(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m\;.
   444		\end{equation}
   445		The vector $v$ is called a \emph{direction} of $\ell(u,v)$; the case $v = 0$
   446		is explicitly allowed, in which case the line is the singleton $\{u\}$. A
   447		line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate
   448		$i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ for which $v = e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   449		vector of $\F_q^m$; such a line is said to be \emph{parallel to the $i$-th
   450		direction}. A line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists
   451		$i \in \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ such that $v_1 = v_2 = \dots = v_i = 0$ (for
   452		$i = 0$ the condition is vacuous, so every line is diagonal).
   453	\end{definition}
   454	
   455	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:line-equiv}
   456		\uses{def:line}
   457		Let $u, v \in \F_q^m$. Then for all $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, we have
   458		$\ell(u,v) = \ell(u',v)$.
   459	\end{proposition}
   460	\begin{proof}
   461		\uses{def:line}
   462		Fix $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, so $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$. Any
   463		$a \in \ell(u,v)$ has the form $a = u + sv = u' + (s - t)v$, so
   464		$\ell(u,v) \subseteq \ell(u',v)$. The symmetric argument gives the reverse
   465		inclusion.
   466	\end{proof}
   467	
   468	Thus, for a fixed direction, a line is an equivalence class of its points: the
   469	pair $(u,v)$ representing it can use any base point on the line. A canonical
   470	representation is obtained as follows.
   471	
   472	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]\label{def:line-representative}
   473		\uses{def:line, def:cl-canonical, prop:line-equiv}
   474		Let $\ell$ be a line in direction $v \neq 0$, and let
   475		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   476		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$
   477		(Definition~\ref{def:cl-canonical}). The \emph{canonical representative of
   478		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   479		\[
   480			u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u) \qquad \text{for all } u \in \ell\;.
   481		\]
   482		This is well defined: since the image and kernel of $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ are
   483		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   484		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and
   485		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u_0) = u_0$; moreover any two points of $\ell$ differ by
   486		a multiple of $v$ and therefore have the same image under
   487		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$. A line $\ell = \ell(u,v)$ is henceforth canonically
   488		represented by the pair $(u_0, v)$. (For $v = 0$, where the singleton
   489		$\{u\}$ leaves no independent kernel basis, we take $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_0$ to
   490		be the identity---the canonical linear map with empty kernel basis---so
   491		that $u_0 = u$; the source leaves this case implicit.)
   492	\end{definition}

   498	\begin{definition}[State space of a linear register]\label{def:lin-reg}
   499		\uses{def:complementary}
   500		For a set $V$, we write $\C^V$ for the complex vector space of dimension
   501		$|V|$, endowed with the canonical orthonormal basis
   502		$\{\ket{x}\}_{x \in V}$. A \emph{quantum state on $V$} is a unit vector
   503		$\ket{\psi}_V \in \C^V$. If $V = \bigoplus_{i=1}^k V_i$ is a direct sum of
   504		subspaces over $\F$, then $\C^V$ is identified with
   505		$\bigotimes_{i=1}^k \C^{V_i}$ by identifying
   506		$\ket{x_1 \oplus \dots \oplus x_k}$ with
   507		$\ket{x_1} \ot \dots \ot \ket{x_k}$. In particular, a basis $\{e_i\}$ of
   508		$V$ yields the decomposition $V = \bigoplus_{i=1}^k (\F e_i)$ and hence
   509		$\C^V = \bigotimes_{i=1}^k \C^{|\F|}$; the factors $\C^{|\F|}$ are called
   510		the \emph{qudits} of $\C^V$.
   511	\end{definition}
   512	
   513	\begin{definition}[EPR state]\label{def:EPR}
   514		\uses{def:lin-reg}
   515		For a linear space $V$ over a finite field $\F$, the \emph{EPR state} on
   516		$\C^V \ot \C^V$ is
   517		\[
   518			\ket{\mathrm{EPR}}_V
   519			= \frac{1}{\sqrt{|V|}} \sum_{x \in V} \ket{x} \ot \ket{x}\;.
   520		\]
   521		We write $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ for $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}}_{\F_q}$ and
   522		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}}$ for $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$.
   523	\end{definition}

   181	
   182	\begin{definition}[Coordinate map and multiplication tables]\label{def:subfields-kappa}
   183		% The source lets k range over all integers; the extension field exists
   184		% only for k >= 1, so that domain condition is made explicit here.
   185		Let $q$ be a prime power and $k \ge 1$ an integer, so that $\F_q$ is a
   186		subfield of $\F_{q^k}$ and $\F_{q^k}$ is a linear space of dimension $k$
   187		over $\F_q$.
   188		Fix a basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$. The bijection
   189		$\kappa_q : \F_{q^k} \to \F_q^k$ associated with this basis is
   190		\[
   191			\kappa_q : a \mapsto (a_i)_{i=1}^k\;, \qquad
   192			\text{where } a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i\;.
   193		\]
   194		The map $\kappa_q$ is an isomorphism of $\F_q$-vector spaces; in particular
   195		$\kappa_q(a + b) = \kappa_q(a) + \kappa_q(b)$ for all $a, b \in \F_{q^k}$.
   196		Moreover, multiplication by a fixed element corresponds to a linear map:
   197		for every $a \in \F_{q^k}$ there is a matrix $K_a \in \Mat_k(\F_q)$, the
   198		\emph{multiplication table of $a$ with respect to $\{e_i\}$}, such that
   199		$\kappa_q(ab) = K_a\, \kappa_q(b)$ for all $b \in \F_{q^k}$.
   200		The map extends coordinatewise to vectors, matrices, and sets: for
   201		$v = (v_1, \dots, v_n) \in \F_{q^k}^n$ set
   202		$\kappa_q(v) = (\kappa_q(v_i))_{i=1}^n \in \F_q^{kn}$; for
   203		$M = (M_{i,j}) \in \Mat_{m,n}(\F_{q^k})$ let
   204		$\chi_q(M) \in \Mat_{mk,nk}(\F_q)$ be the block matrix whose $(i,j)$-th
   205		block is $K_{M_{i,j}}$; and for a set $S$ of vectors put
   206		$\kappa_q(S) = \{\kappa_q(v) : v \in S\}$. When $q = p$ is the field
   207		characteristic, the subscript is omitted and we write $\kappa$ and $\chi$.
   208	\end{definition}
   209	
   210	\begin{definition}[Admissible field size]\label{def:admissible-size}
   211		A field size $q$ is \emph{admissible} if $q = 2^k$ for an odd integer $k$.
   212	\end{definition}
   213	
   214	Only fields $\F_{2^k}$ with $k$ odd are used in the analysis of the Pauli basis
   215	test.
   216	
   217	\begin{definition}[Trace of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$]\label{def:subfield-trace}
   218		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:admissible-size}
   219		The \emph{trace of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$} is the map
   220		% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
   221		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-trace}
   222			\tr_{q^k \to q} : a \mapsto \Tr(K_a)
   223		\end{equation}
   224		for $a \in \F_{q^k}$, where $K_a$ is the multiplication table of $a$ with
   225		respect to the basis $\{e_i\}$. The trace is an $\F_q$-linear map from
   226		$\F_{q^k}$ to $\F_q$, and it is independent of the choice of basis, as can
   227		be seen from the equivalent formula
   228		\[
   229			\tr_{q^k \to q}(a) = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} a^{q^j}\;.
   230		\]
   231		For admissible $q = 2^k$ we use the shorthand $\tr$ for $\tr_{q \to 2}$.
   232	\end{definition}
   233	
   234	\begin{definition}[Dual, self-dual, and normal bases]\label{def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   235		\uses{def:subfield-trace}
   236		A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', \dots, e_k'\}$ of a basis
   237		$\{e_1, \dots, e_k\}$ of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$ is a basis such that
   238		$\tr_{q^k \to q}(e^{}_i e'_j) = \delta_{i,j}$ for all
   239		$i, j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$. A \emph{self-dual basis} is one equal to its own
   240		dual. If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set
   241		$\{\alpha^{q^j}\}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$, that
   242		basis is called a \emph{normal basis}. Self-dual and normal bases do not
   243		exist for every field extension, but for $q = 2$ and odd $k$ a self-dual
   244		normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ always exists; \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}
   245		exhibits one through an explicit construction.
   246	\end{definition}
   247	
   248	\begin{lemma}[Coordinate maps of self-dual bases]\label{lem:downsize_field}
   249		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace,
   250			def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis, def:dot-product-orthogonal}
   251		Let $q$ be a prime power, $k \ge 1$ an integer, and $\{e_i\}$ a self-dual
   252		basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$. The map $\kappa_q$ corresponding to
   253		$\{e_i\}$ satisfies:
   254		\begin{enumerate}
   255			\item for all $x \in \F_{q^k}$,
   256			      $\kappa_q(x) = \bigl(\tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_1), \dots,
   257			      \tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_k)\bigr)$;
   258			\item for all $x, y \in \F_{q^k}$,
   259			      $\tr_{q^k \to q}(xy) = \kappa_q(x) \cdot \kappa_q(y)$;
   260			\item for all $M \in \Mat_{m,n}(\F_{q^k})$ and $v \in \F_{q^k}^n$,
   261			      $\chi_q(M)\, \kappa_q(v) = \kappa_q(Mv)$.
   262		\end{enumerate}
   263		Items 1 and 2 use self-duality; item 3 holds for an arbitrary basis.
   264	\end{lemma}
   265	\begin{proof}
   266		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace, def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   267		For item 1, write $x = \sum_i x_i e_i$, multiply both sides by $e_j$, and
   268		take traces: $\tr_{q^k \to q}(x e_j) = \sum_i x_i \tr_{q^k \to q}(e_i e_j)
   269		= x_j$ by self-duality. For item 2, expand
   270		$xy = \sum_{i,j} x_i y_j e_i e_j$ and take traces; self-duality retains
   271		exactly the diagonal terms, giving $\sum_i x_i y_i = \kappa_q(x) \cdot
   272		\kappa_q(y)$. For item 3, the $i$-th block of $\kappa_q(Mv)$ equals
   273		$\sum_j \kappa_q(M_{i,j} v_j) = \sum_j K_{M_{i,j}}\, \kappa_q(v_j)$, which
   274		is the $i$-th block row of $\chi_q(M)$ applied to $\kappa_q(v)$.
   275	\end{proof}
   276	
   277	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:one}
   278		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:subfield-trace, def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   279		Let $k$ be an odd integer and $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ a self-dual normal basis of
   280		$\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$. Then $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i$, and the
   281		representation $\kappa(1)$ of the unit $1 \in \F_{2^k}$ is the all-ones
   282		vector in $\F_2^k$.
   283	\end{lemma}
   284	\begin{proof}
   285		\uses{lem:downsize_field}
   286		Normality gives $e_{i+1} = e_i^2$ (indices taken cyclically), and
   287		$\tr(b^2) = \tr(b)$ for every $b \in \F_{2^k}$ because squaring permutes the
   288		terms of $\tr(b) = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} b^{2^j}$, using $b^{2^k} = b$. Hence all
   289		the values $\tr(e_i)$ coincide. If the common value were $0$, then $\tr$
   290		would vanish identically on $\F_{2^k}$ by linearity; but then item 1 of
   291		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} would give $\kappa(b) =
   292		(\tr(b e_1), \dots, \tr(b e_k)) = 0$ for every $b$, contradicting the
   293		bijectivity of $\kappa$. Thus $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i$, and item 1 of
   294		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   295		$\kappa(1) = (\tr(e_1), \dots, \tr(e_k)) = (1, \dots, 1)$.
   296	\end{proof}

   298	\begin{definition}[Binary representation of field elements]\label{def:binary-representation}
   299		\uses{def:subfields-kappa, def:admissible-size,
   300			def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis}
   301		Let $q = 2^k$ be an admissible field size. For each odd $k$ we fix, once and
   302		for all, a self-dual normal basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{2^k}$ over
   303		$\F_2$ together with its multiplication tables
   304		$\{K_{e_i}\}_{i=1}^k$ (Definition~\ref{def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis});
   305		the maps $\kappa$ and $\tr$ always refer to this basis. The \emph{binary
   306		representation} of $a \in \F_{2^k}$ is the $k$-bit string
   307		$\kappa(a) \in \F_2^k$, the \emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}; the two are
   308		freely identified. Addition of representations is bitwise addition modulo
   309		$2$, and multiplication is determined by the multiplication tables through
   310		\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-mult}
   311			\kappa(ab) = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i\, \kappa(e_i b)
   312			= \sum_{i=1}^k a_i \bigl(K_{e_i}\, \kappa(b)\bigr)\;,
   313		\end{equation}
   314		where $\kappa(a) = (a_i)_{i=1}^k$.
   315	\end{definition}

   119	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   125	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/

   127	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   128	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   129	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)

   139	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=

   142	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)

   150	intentionally not asserted here.

   152	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   153	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))

    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))

    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :

    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    59	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    61	-/
    62	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    63	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    64	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)

    70	
    71	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    72	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    73	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    74	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.

    77	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    78	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    79	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    80	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    81	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    82	
    83	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    84	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.

    93	
    94	/--

     5	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     6	
     7	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     8	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     9	estimates to later proof stages.

    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    16	-/

    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    25	/--
    26	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    27	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    29	-/
    30	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    31	    [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    33	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    34	
    35	/--
    36	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    37	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    38	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    39	-/
    40	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    41	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    42	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    43	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    44	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    45	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)

   209	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())
   210	
   211	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   212	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   213	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   214	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   217	-/
   218	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   219	  | .point _ => 1
   220	  | .aline _ => 2
   221	  | .dline _ => 3
   222	  | .pauli _ => 0
   223	  | .pairW _ => 1
   224	  | .pair => 1
   225	  | .ms _ => 1
   226	
   227	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   228	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   229	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   230	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   231	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   235	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   236	  match t with
   237	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   238	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   239	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   240	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   241	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   242	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   243	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   244	
   245	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   246	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   247	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   248	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   249	-/
   250	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   251	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   252	  sorry
   253	
   254	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   255	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   256	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   258	-/
   259	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   260	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   261	  let lineEdges :=
   262	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   263	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   264	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   265	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   266	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   267	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   268	  let basisEdges :=
   269	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   270	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   271	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   272	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   273	  let pairEdges :=
   274	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   275	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   276	  let msEdges' :=
   277	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   278	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   279	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   280	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   281	
   282	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   283	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   284	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   285	-/
   286	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   287	
   288	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   289	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   290	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   291	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   292	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   293	-/
   294	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   295	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   296	
   297	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   298	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   299	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   300	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   301	-/
   302	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   303	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   304	  simp [pauliEdges]
   305	
   306	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,
   307	then applying the endpoint CL maps.  This is the inlined typed-CL construction
   308	of `def:pauli-question-distribution` (blueprint lines 285-329; paper
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   310	-/
   311	noncomputable def pauliQuestionSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   312	    Finset (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   313	  by
   314	    classical
   315	    exact
   316	      (Finset.univ.filter fun s : (PauliType × PauliType) × PauliSpace P =>
   317	          Sym2.mk s.1.1 s.1.2 ∈ pauliEdges).image (fun s =>
   318	        ((s.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   319	
   320	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   321	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   322	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   323	-/
   324	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   325	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   326	  by
   327	    classical
   328	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   329	    exact
   330	      Distribution.map

1	import Mathlib
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.CondLinear
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs
     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    76	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    78	-/
    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80	
    81	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97	
    98	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   100	
   101	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   102	
   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   122	
   123	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate
   135	
   136	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

231	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   232	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   233	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   234	-/
   235	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   236	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   237	  toFun
   238	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   239	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   240	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   241	  invFun
   242	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   243	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   244	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   245	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   246	  right_inv := by
   247	    intro x
   248	    cases x with
   249	    | inl a => rfl
   250	    | inr x =>
   251	        cases x with
   252	        | inl a => rfl
   253	        | inr a => rfl
   254	
   255	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   256	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   257	
   258	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   259	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   260	
   261	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   262	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   263	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   264	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   265	-/
   266	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   267	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   268	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   269	
   270	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   271	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   272	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   273	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   274	-/
   275	def validLdAnswer (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   276	  match t, a with
   277	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   278	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   279	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   280	  | _, _ => false
   281	
   282	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   283	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   284	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   285	-/
   286	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   287	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   288	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   289	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   290	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   291	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   292	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   293	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   294	
   295	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   296	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   297	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   298	-/
   299	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   300	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   301	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   307	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   308	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   310	-/
   311	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   312	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   313	  open Classical in
   314	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   315	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   316	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   317	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   318	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   319	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   320	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   321	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   322	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   328	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   329	      else false
   330	
   331	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   332	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   333	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   334	-/
   335	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   336	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   337	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   338	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   339	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   340	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   341	  μ_prob := by sorry
   342	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   343	
   344	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import Mathlib
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.FieldBasis
     3	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic
     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     7	
     8	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     9	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
    10	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    11	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    16	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    28	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    29	
    30	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    31	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    33	-/
    34	inductive PauliKind where
    35	  | X
    36	  | Z
    37	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    38	
    39	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    40	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    41	
    42	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    43	character in their statement types. -/
    44	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    45	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    46	
    47	/--
    48	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    49	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    51	-/
    52	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    53	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    54	
    55	/--
    56	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    57	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    61	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    62	
    63	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    64	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    65	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    66	  match W with
    67	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    68	  | .X =>
    69	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    70	
    71	/--
    72	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    73	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.

   336	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   337	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,

   340	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   341	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   342	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   343	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   344	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   345	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   346	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   347	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   348	  deriving DecidableEq

   350	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   351	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   352	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   353	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   354	-/
   355	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   356	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   357	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   358	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   359	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   360	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   361	
   362	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   363	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   364	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   365	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   366	-/
   367	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   368	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   369	  toFun
   370	    | .value a => .inl a
   371	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   372	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   373	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   374	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   375	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   376	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   377	  invFun
   378	    | .inl a => .value a
   379	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   380	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   381	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   382	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   383	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   384	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   385	  left_inv := by
   386	    intro x
   387	    cases x <;> rfl
   388	  right_inv := by
   389	    intro x
   390	    cases x with
   391	    | inl a => rfl
   392	    | inr x =>
   393	        cases x with
   394	        | inl a => rfl
   395	        | inr x =>
   396	            cases x with
   397	            | inl a => rfl
   398	            | inr x =>
   399	                cases x with
   400	                | inl a => rfl
   401	                | inr x =>
   402	                    cases x with
   403	                    | inl a => rfl
   404	                    | inr x =>
   405	                        cases x with
   406	                        | inl a => rfl
   407	                        | inr a => rfl

   410	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
