   412	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   413	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   414	
   415	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   416	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   417	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   418	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   419	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   420	-/
   421	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   440	-/
   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   482	-/
   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      if tA = tB then
   534	        decide (a = b)
   535	      else
   536	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   537	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   538	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   539	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   540	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   541	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   542	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   543	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   544	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   545	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   546	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   547	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   548	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   549	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   550	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   551	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   552	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   553	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   554	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   555	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   556	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   557	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   563	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   564	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   565	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   566	          else true
   567	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   568	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   569	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   570	          else true
   571	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   572	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   573	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   574	          else true
   575	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   576	    else false
   577	
   578	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   579	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   580	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   581	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   582	-/
   583	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   584	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   585	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   586	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   587	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   588	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   589	  μ_prob := by sorry
   590	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   591	
   592	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

198	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   199	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   200	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   201	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   202	-/
   203	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   204	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   205	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   206	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   207	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   208	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   209	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   210	
   211	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   212	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   213	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   214	-/
   215	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   216	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   217	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   218	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   219	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   220	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   221	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   222	
   223	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   224	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   225	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem is stated over
   226	the fixed self-dual-normal field model stored in `AdmissibleParams`, not over a
   227	freshly quantified field identification.  Blueprint
   228	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   229	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   230	
   231	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   232	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   233	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   234	-/
   235	theorem pauli_soundness :
   236	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   237	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   238	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   239	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   240	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   241	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   242	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   243	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   244	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   245	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   246	  sorry
   247

    29	/-- Parameters for the low-degree game, including the fixed field model used by
    30	the ambient coefficient space.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:ld-game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    33	-/
    34	structure LdParams where
    35	  q : ℕ
    36	  m : ℕ
    37	  d : ℕ
    38	  k : ℕ
    39	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    40	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    41	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	  model : FixedFieldModel q
    45	
    46	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    47	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper
    48	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    49	-/
    50	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := P.model.K
    51	
    52	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    55	-/
    56	inductive LdType where
    57	  | point
    58	  | aline
    59	  | dline
    60	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    61	
    62	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    63	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    65	-/
    66	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    67	
    68	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    71	-/
    72	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    73	
    74	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    76	-/
    77	def LdSpace.point (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    78	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    79	
    80	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    82	-/
    83	def LdSpace.seed (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    84	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    85	
    86	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    88	-/
    89	def LdSpace.direction (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    90	  fun i => z (.inr i)
    91	
    92	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
    93	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    94	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
    98	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
    99	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   100	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   101	
   102	/-- The source uses the block quotient of the fixed integer representation.  The
   103	`Fin.ofNat` wrapper supplies the totalized boundary behavior for the temporary
   104	 skeleton's proof-irrelevant zero-dimension branch.  This is the projection
   105	 clause of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   106	 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   107	 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   108	-/
   109	def prefixProjection (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   110	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   111	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   112	
   113	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   114	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   117	-/
   118	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   119	  fun i => match i with
   120	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   121	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   122	  | .inr _ => 0
   123	
   124	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   125	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   126	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   127	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   128	-/
   129	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   130	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   131	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   132	  fun i => match i with
   133	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   134	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   135	  | .inr _ => 0
   136	
   137	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   138	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   139	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   140	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   141	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   142	-/
   143	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   144	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   145	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr j => direction j
   151	
   152	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   153	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   154	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   155	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   156	-/
   157	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   158	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   159	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   160	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   161	
   162	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   163	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   164	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   165	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   166	-/
   167	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   168	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   172	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   173	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   174	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   175	-/
   176	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   177	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   178	  sorry
   179	
   180	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   181	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   183	-/
   184	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   185	
   186	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   187	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
   188	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   189	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   190	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   191	-/
   192	noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
   193	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   194	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   195	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   196	
   197	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   198	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   199	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   202	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   203	  Distribution.map
   204	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   205	    (fun s =>
   206	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   207	
   208	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   209	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   210	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   211	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   212	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   213	-/
   214	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   215	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   218	  deriving DecidableEq
   219	
   220	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   221	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   222	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   223	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   224	-/
   225	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   226	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   228	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   229	
   230	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   231	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   232	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   233	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   234	-/
   235	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   236	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   237	  toFun
   238	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   239	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   240	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   241	  invFun
   242	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   243	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   244	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   245	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   246	  right_inv := by
   247	    intro x
   248	    cases x with
   249	    | inl a => rfl
   250	    | inr x =>
   251	        cases x with
   252	        | inl a => rfl
   253	        | inr a => rfl
   254	
   255	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   256	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   257	
   258	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   259	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   260	
   261	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   262	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   263	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   264	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   265	-/
   266	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   267	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   268	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   269	
   270	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   271	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   272	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   273	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   274	-/
   275	def validLdAnswer (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   276	  match t, a with
   277	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   278	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   279	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   280	  | _, _ => false
   281	
   282	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   283	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   284	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   285	-/
   286	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   287	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   288	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   289	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   290	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   291	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   292	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   293	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   294	
   295	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   296	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   297	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   298	-/
   299	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   300	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   301	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   307	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   308	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   310	-/
   311	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   312	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   313	  open Classical in
   314	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   315	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   316	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   317	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   318	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   319	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   320	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   321	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   322	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   328	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   329	      else false
   330	
   331	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   332	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   333	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   334	-/
   335	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   336	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   337	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   338	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   339	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   340	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   341	  μ_prob := by sorry
   342	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   343	
   344	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import Mathlib

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    76	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    78	-/
    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80	
    81	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97	
    98	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   100	
   101	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   102	
   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   122	
   123	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate
   135	
   136	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   176	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   177	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing

   186	      match W with
   187	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   188	      | .Z => 0
   189	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   190	      match W with
   191	      | .X => 0
   192	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   193	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   195	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   196	  | .inr _ => 0

   207	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   208	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   209	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   211	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   212	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   213	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the

   218	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   219	  | .point _ => 1
   220	  | .aline _ => 2
   221	  | .dline _ => 3
   222	  | .pauli _ => 0
   223	  | .pairW _ => 1
   224	  | .pair => 1
   225	  | .ms _ => 1

   227	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   228	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   229	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This

   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

   234	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   235	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   236	  match t with
   237	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   238	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   239	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   240	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   241	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   242	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   243	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection

   254	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   255	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   256	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   258	-/
   259	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   260	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   261	  let lineEdges :=
   262	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   263	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   264	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   265	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   266	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   267	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   268	  let basisEdges :=
   269	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   270	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   271	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   272	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   273	  let pairEdges :=
   274	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   275	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   276	  let msEdges' :=
   277	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   278	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   279	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   280	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   281	
   282	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   283	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   284	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   286	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P

   288	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   289	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   290	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   291	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   292	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   293	-/
   294	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   295	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   296	
   297	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   298	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   299	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   300	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   301	-/
   302	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   303	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   304	  simp [pauliEdges]
   305	
   306	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,
   307	then applying the endpoint CL maps.  This is the inlined typed-CL construction
   308	of `def:pauli-question-distribution` (blueprint lines 285-329; paper
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   311	noncomputable def pauliQuestionSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   312	    Finset (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   313	  by
   314	    classical
   315	    exact
   316	      (Finset.univ.filter fun s : (PauliType × PauliType) × PauliSpace P =>
   317	          Sym2.mk s.1.1 s.1.2 ∈ pauliEdges).image (fun s =>
   318	        ((s.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   319	
   320	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   321	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   322	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   323	-/
   324	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   325	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   326	  by
   327	    classical
   328	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   329	    exact
   330	      Distribution.map

331	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   332	        (fun s =>
   333	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   334	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

   336	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   337	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   338	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   339	-/
   340	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   341	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   342	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   343	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   344	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   345	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   346	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   347	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   348	  deriving DecidableEq
   349	
   350	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   351	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   352	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   353	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   354	-/
   355	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   356	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   357	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   358	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   359	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   360	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   361	
   362	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   363	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   364	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   365	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   366	-/
   367	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   368	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   369	  toFun
   370	    | .value a => .inl a
   371	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   372	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   373	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   374	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   375	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   376	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   377	  invFun
   378	    | .inl a => .value a
   379	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   380	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   381	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   382	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   383	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   384	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   385	  left_inv := by
   386	    intro x
   387	    cases x <;> rfl
   388	  right_inv := by
   389	    intro x
   390	    cases x with
   391	    | inl a => rfl
   392	    | inr x =>
   393	        cases x with
   394	        | inl a => rfl
   395	        | inr x =>
   396	            cases x with
   397	            | inl a => rfl
   398	            | inr x =>
   399	                cases x with
   400	                | inl a => rfl
   401	                | inr x =>

# MIPStarRE-local convention addenda

The canonical convention documents live in the `lean-conventions` skill of
[texra-ai/texra-lean-skills](https://github.com/texra-ai/texra-lean-skills)
(auto-installed for Claude Code sessions via `.claude/settings.json`; other
agents: clone the repository and symlink the skill directories, per its
README). This file holds only
MIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared
rules never move here.

## Style (MATHLIB_style)

### Linter warnings

Do not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add
broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide
blocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real
maintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.

Fix the warning at its source whenever possible:

- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;
- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass
  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;
- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;
- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than
  silencing `linter.flexible`.

If a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting
exception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably
`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.
Such exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as
the main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.

## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)

### Source-faithfulness checks

For this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean
statement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before
applying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions
`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed
source-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the
corresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.

Reject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,
repair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,
or arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as
positivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal
encodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when
mathematically load-bearing.

Reviewers should also inspect `\lean{}` and `\leanok` links.  A source-labelled
blueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction
theorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.
Auxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the
remark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.

## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)

### Companion document

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the
> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

### Project paper-realignment protocol

The canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions
`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as
follows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in
`AGENTS.md`):

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be
> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

### Axiom policy

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

### Source-statement proof gaps

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.
# Formalization Patterns

Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the
gap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.

This document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the
Lean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize
these patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits
in `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:
`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the
proof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.

## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations

### The rule

A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.

The project therefore distinguishes three objects.

| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
|--------|------------------|------------------|
| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |

It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
conditional helper is given a different name.

The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
of a source-labelled theorem.

### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily

| Temporary reason | Explanation |
|------------------|-------------|
| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.

  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$

  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\

1	\section{Classical and Quantum Low-degree Tests}
     2	\label{sec:ldt}
     3	
     4	In this section we introduce the classical and quantum low individual degree tests, that form the basis of our classical, quantum-sound and quantum PCP constructions. For quantum soundness of the classical test we refer to~\cite{ML20}. For the quantum test, we refer to~\cite{natarajan2018low} and its adaptation to the low individual degree test given in Appendix~\ref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
     5	The protocol in this work combines both of these tests, using the quantum
     6	low individual degree test for question reduction and the classical low individual degree test for
     7	answer reduction.
     8	Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier} below introduces the classical test,
     9	and Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier} does the same for the quantum 
    10	test.
    11	Prior to doing this, we introduce the \emph{Magic Square game} in
    12	Section~\ref{sec:ms}, a key subroutine in the quantum test.
    13	
    14	
    15	\subsection{The classical low-degree test}
    16	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    17	
    18	We begin with a generalization of the classical low-degree test known as the
    19	``simultaneous individual low-degree test''.
    20	We sometimes refer to this as the ``classical low-degree test'' for short.
    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see
    22	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) as well as the answer-reduction normal form
    23	verifier (see Section~\ref{sec:ans}).
    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
    25	that the question distribution can be implemented as a (typed) conditionally
    26	linear distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL
    27	distributions).
    28	
    29	
    30	\subsubsection{The game}
    31	\label{sec:ld-game}
    32	
    33	The game $\game^\ld$ is parametrized by a tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
    34	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
    35	and $m$ divides $q$.
    36	We sometimes write $\game^\ld_\ldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
    37	classical low-degree test on the parameter tuple $\ldparams$.
    38	
    39	We first provide a high-level description of the game for $k=1$.
    40	It is based on the low-individual degree variant of the multilinearity test
    41	of~\cite{babai1991non}, where one player (called the ``points player'') receives
    42	a random point $u \in \F_q^m$, and the other player (called the ``lines
    43	player'') receives a random axis-parallel line $\line$ that contains $u$, i.e.\
    44	the line parallel to the $i$-th axis which goes through point $u$, for uniformly
    45	random $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
    46	The points player is supposed to respond with a value $a \in \F_q$, and the
    47	lines player is supposed to respond with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of
    48	degree at most $d$ such that $f_\line(u_i) = a$, where $u_i$ is the $i$-th
    49	coordinate of $u$.
    50	
    51	Suppose the players agree beforehand on a global polynomial $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$
    52	such that every variable has degree at most $d$.
    53	Then a winning strategy is the following: the points player responds with
    54	$g(u)$, and the lines player responds with the univariate polynomial $f_\line$
    55	that is the restriction of $g$ to line $\line$; formally, for $t \in \F_q$,
    56	\[f_\line(t)=g(u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{i-1},t,u_{i+1},\ldots,u_m)\;.\] It is easy to
    57	see that $f_\line(t)$ has degree at most $d$ in the variable $t$.
    58	Thus in this case the players will pass the low-degree test with probability
    59	$1$.
    60	The low-degree testing theorem states that the converse approximately holds: if
    61	the players pass the low-degree test with probability close to $1$, then their
    62	responses must be approximately consistent (in some sense) with a global
    63	polynomial $g$ with individual degree $d$.
    64	
    65	When $k > 1$, the players are supposed to respond with a \emph{tuple} of
    66	answers; and the test is intended to check that the players' responses are
    67	consistent with a $k$-tuple of functions $g_i: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ that are
    68	polynomials where every variable has degree at most $d$.
    69	
    70	The game that we use is slightly more elaborate than the ``axis-parallel
    71	lines-versus-points'' test just described.
    72	In addition, we have two other subtests.
    73	One is a ``diagonal line-vs-points'' test: here, the points player receives a
    74	point $u \in \F_q^m$ as before, but the lines player receives a line $\line$
    75	that goes through $u$ but is not necessarily axis-aligned.
    76	Instead, it's chosen by first picking an index $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$
    77	uniformly at random, picking $v \in \F_q^m$ uniformly at random, and letting $v'
    78	= \pi_{i-1}(v) = (0,0,\ldots,0,v_i,v_{i+1},\ldots,v_m)$ (i.e., $\pi_{i-1}$
    79	zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input).
    80	Then, the line is defined as the set
    81	\[
    82		\line = \{ u + tv' : t \in \F_q \}\;,
    83	\]
    84	which is a uniformly random line in the affine subspace of $\F^m_q$
    85	corresponding to all points $v$ whose first $(i-1)$ coordinates match those of
    86	$u$.
    87	The points player responds with a value $a \in \F_q$, the lines player responds
    88	with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of degree $md$,\footnote{Since $\line$ is
    89	  no longer axis-parallel, the restriction of an individual degree-$d$
    90	  polynomial $g$ to a line $\line$ may yield a degree $md$ polynomial.}
    91	and the verifier checks that $f_\line(t_u) = a$ (where $t_u \in \F_q$ is the
    92	projection of $u$ onto the line $\line$ with respect to a canonical
    93	parameterization of $\line$).
    94	
    95	The other additional test is a ``consistency test'', where both players receive
    96	either the same points question, the same axis-parallel lines question, or the
    97	same diagonal lines question.
    98	In all cases they are expected to respond with the same answer.
    99

   263	\section{The Pauli basis test}
   264	% Paper label sec:qld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
   265	\label{sec:qld-game}
   266	
   267	The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

512	\subsection{The Magic Square game}
   513	\label{sec:ms}
   514	
   515	We recall the \emph{Magic Square game} of Mermin and
   516	Peres~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible,aravind2002simple}.
   517	The Magic Square game is a simple self-test for EPR pairs (it tests for two of
   518	them). In addition, it allows one to test that a pair of observables
   519	\emph{anticommutes}.
   520	Here we use it as a building block to construct the quantum low-degree test. 
   521	
   522	There are several formulations of the Magic Square game; here we present it as a
   523	\emph{binary constraint satisfaction} game~\cite{cleve2014characterization}.
   524	In this formulation of the game (denoted by $\game_\MS$) there are $6$ linear
   525	equations defined over $9$ variables that take values in $\F_2$.
   526	The variables correspond to the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid, as depicted in
   527	Figure~\ref{fig:ms}.
   528	Five of the equations correspond to the constraint that the sum of the variables
   529	in each row and the first two columns must be equal to $0$, and the last
   530	equation requires that the sum of the variables in the last column must be equal
   531	to $1$.
   532	
   533	\begin{figure}[ht!]
   534		\begin{center}
   535	    \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.6}
   536			\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
   537				\hline
   538				$x_1$ & $x_2$ & $x_3$ \\
   539				\hline 
   540				$x_4$ & $x_5$ & $x_6$ \\	
   541				\hline
   542				$x_7$ & $x_8$ & $x_9$ \\
   543				\hline
   544			\end{tabular}
   545			\caption{The Magic Square game}
   546			\label{fig:ms}
   547			\end{center}
   548	\end{figure}
   549	
   550	The question set $\type^\ms$ of the Magic Square game is the following:
   551	\begin{equation*}
   552	  \begin{split}
   553	    \type^\msc & = \{ \Constraint_i : i = 1, 2, \ldots, 6\}\;,\\
   554	    \type^\msv & = \{ \Variable_j : j = 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\;,\\
   555	    \type^\ms & = \type^\msc \cup \type^\msv\;.
   556	  \end{split}
   557	\end{equation*}
   558	The questions $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ correspond to the three row
   559	constraints, the questions $\Constraint_4$, $\Constraint_5$ correspond to the first
   560	two column constraints, and question $\Constraint_6$ corresponds to the third
   561	column constraint.
   562	
   563	In the Magic Square game, the verifier first samples a constraint $\Constraint_i
   564	\in \type^\msc$ uniformly at random, and then samples $\Variable_j$, one of the
   565	three variables in the row or column corresponding to $\Constraint_i$, uniformly
   566	at random.
   567	One player is randomly assigned to be the $\Constraint$ player, and the other is
   568	assigned to be the $\Variable$ player.
   569	The $\Constraint$ player is sent the question $\Constraint_i$ and is expected to
   570	respond with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$,
   571	where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables corresponding to
   572	$\Constraint_i$.
   573	The $\Variable$ player is given question $\Variable_j$ and is expected to
   574	respond with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$.
   575	The players win if the $\Constraint$ player's answers satisfy the equation
   576	associated with $\Constraint_i$, and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   577	More precisely, the verifier samples an edge of the type graph (see Section~\ref{sec:types}) $G^\ms$
   578	in Fig.~\ref{fig:type-graph-ms}, sends one endpoint to a random player, and the
   579	other endpoint to the other player.

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.

     8	Tensor-sum commutation, positivity/boundedness preservation,
     9	factoring lemmas, and sandwich-residual estimates used in
    10	the main induction step and polynomial-agreement arguments.
    11	-/
    12	
    13	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    14	
    15	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    16	
    17	/-! ### Tensor-placement helper lemmas -/
    18	
    19	/-- Left tensor placement commutes with finite sums. -/
    20	theorem leftTensor_finset_sum {α : Type*}
    21	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
    22	    (s : Finset α) (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) :
    23	    Finset.sum s (fun a => leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (f a)) =
    24	      leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (Finset.sum s f) := by
    25	  classical
    26	  simpa [leftTensor, opTensor] using
    27	    (opTensor_sum_left_finset (s := s) (f := f)
    28	      (B := (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂))).symm
    29	
    30	/-- Left tensor placement commutes with operator averages. -/
    31	theorem leftTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution {α : Type*}
    32	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
    33	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) :
    34	    leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A) =
    35	      averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (A a)) := by
    36	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution
    37	  rw [← leftTensor_finset_sum (ι₂ := ι₂) 𝒟.support
    38	    (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • A a)]
    39	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    40	  intro a _
    41	  simpa [leftTensor, opTensor] using
    42	    (opTensor_smul_left_error
    43	      (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) (𝒟.weight a) (A a) (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂))
    44	
    45	/-- Expanding the left-tensor mass of a submeasurement on a bipartite state as
    46	the sum of per-outcome left-tensor expectations.
    47	
    48	This is a generic identity at the level of `ev ψ (leftTensor _)`: applying
    49	`SubMeas.sum_eq_total`, pulling `leftTensor` through the finite sum via
    50	`leftTensor_finset_sum`, and distributing `ev` through the sum via
    51	`ev_finset_sum`. Using the definitional equalities
    52	`subMeasMass ψ A.liftLeft = ev ψ A.liftLeft.total = ev ψ (leftTensor A.total)`,
    53	this immediately yields the helper-stage opening
    54	`subMeasMass ψ A.liftLeft = ∑ a, ev ψ (leftTensor (A.outcome a))` used in the
    55	Section 9 / Section 12 calculations. -/
    56	theorem ev_leftTensor_total_eq_sum_outcome {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    57	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    58	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι)) (A : SubMeas α ι) :
    59	    ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι) A.total) =
    60	      ∑ a : α, ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι) (A.outcome a)) := by
    61	  rw [← A.sum_eq_total,
    62	      ← leftTensor_finset_sum (ι₂ := ι) Finset.univ (fun a : α => A.outcome a),
    63	      ev_finset_sum]
    64	
    65	/-- Evaluation of a left-placed operator average is the average of the
    66	left-placed evaluations. -/
    67	theorem ev_leftTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution {α : Type*}
    68	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
    69	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι₁ × ι₂)) (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    70	    (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) :
    71	    ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A)) =
    72	      avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (A a))) := by
    73	  rw [leftTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution]
    74	  exact ev_averageOperatorOverDistribution ψ 𝒟
    75	    (fun a => leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (A a))
    76	
    77	/-- Right tensor placement commutes with finite sums. -/
    78	theorem rightTensor_finset_sum {α : Type*}
    79	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
    80	    (s : Finset α) (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
    81	    Finset.sum s (fun a => rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (f a)) =
    82	      rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (Finset.sum s f) := by
    83	  classical
    84	  simpa [rightTensor, opTensor] using
    85	    (opTensor_sum_right_finset (A := (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁)) (s := s)
    86	      (f := f)).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Right tensor placement commutes with operator averages. -/
    89	theorem rightTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution {α : Type*}
    90	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
    91	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
    92	    rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A) =
    93	      averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (A a)) := by
    94	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution
    95	  rw [← rightTensor_finset_sum (ι₁ := ι₁) 𝒟.support
    96	    (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • A a)]
    97	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    98	  intro a _
    99	  simpa [rightTensor, opTensor] using
   100	    (opTensor_smul_right_error
   101	      (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) (𝒟.weight a) (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (A a))
   102	
   103	/-- Evaluation of a right-placed operator average is the average of the
   104	right-placed evaluations. -/
   105	theorem ev_rightTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution {α : Type*}
   106	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   107	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι₁ × ι₂)) (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   108	    (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   109	    ev ψ (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A)) =
   110	      avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ev ψ (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (A a))) := by
   111	  rw [rightTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution]
   112	  exact ev_averageOperatorOverDistribution ψ 𝒟
   113	    (fun a => rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (A a))
   114	
   115	/-- Tensoring on the right commutes with operator averages in the left factor. -/
   116	theorem opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_left {α ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
   117	    [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   118	    (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   119	    (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   120	    opTensor (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A) B =
   121	      averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => opTensor (A a) B) := by
   122	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution
   123	  rw [opTensor_sum_left_finset]
   124	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   125	  intro a _
   126	  simpa using opTensor_smul_left_error (c := 𝒟.weight a) (A := A a) (B := B)
   127	
   128	/-- Tensoring on the left commutes with operator averages in the right factor. -/
   129	theorem opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_right {α ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
   130	    [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   131	    (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   132	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   133	    opTensor A (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 B) =
   134	      averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 (fun a => opTensor A (B a)) := by
   135	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution
   136	  rw [opTensor_sum_right_finset]
   137	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   138	  intro a _
   139	  simpa using opTensor_smul_right_error (c := 𝒟.weight a) (A := A) (B := B a)
   140	
   141	/-- Evaluation of an averaged left tensor factor is the average of the
   142	corresponding tensor expectations. -/
   143	theorem ev_opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_left {α ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
   144	    [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   145	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι₁ × ι₂)) (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   146	    (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   147	    ev ψ (opTensor (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 A) B) =
   148	      avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ev ψ (opTensor (A a) B)) := by
   149	  rw [opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_left]
   150	  exact ev_averageOperatorOverDistribution ψ 𝒟 (fun a => opTensor (A a) B)
   151	
   152	/-- Evaluation of an averaged right tensor factor is the average of the
   153	corresponding tensor expectations. -/
   154	theorem ev_opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_right {α ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
   155	    [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   156	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι₁ × ι₂)) (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   157	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   158	    ev ψ (opTensor A (averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 B)) =
   159	      avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ev ψ (opTensor A (B a))) := by
   160	  rw [opTensor_averageOperatorOverDistribution_right]
   161	  exact ev_averageOperatorOverDistribution ψ 𝒟 (fun a => opTensor A (B a))
   162	
   163	/-- A complex scalar on the left register factors out of a bipartite tensor product.
   164	
   165	This is the tensor-placement version of bilinearity of `opTensor`: placing
   166	`c • A` on the left and multiplying by the right placement of `B` equals the
   167	same scalar multiplying `leftTensor A * rightTensor B`. -/
   168	theorem leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_smul_left
   169	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   170	    (c : Error) (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   171	    leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) ((c : ℂ) • A) * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) B =
   172	      (c : ℂ) • (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) A * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) B) := by
   173	  rw [leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor, leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor]
   174	  simpa [opTensor] using Matrix.smul_kronecker (c : ℂ) A B
   175	
   176	/-- A complex scalar on the right register factors out of a bipartite tensor product.
   177	
   178	This is the tensor-placement version of bilinearity of `opTensor`: placing
   179	`c • B` on the right and multiplying by the left placement of `A` equals the
   180	same scalar multiplying `leftTensor A * rightTensor B`. -/

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
